  • Hands‑on work on AI products in the last 12 months (LLMs, agents, AI features), with ownership of meaningful parts of the system.

  • Experience with chatbots/conversational AI, RAG and LLM evaluation pipelines.

  • Strong skills in at least one of Go, TypeScript/JavaScript or Python.

What We Offer

Within the range, individual pay is determined by factors including relevant skills, experience, and education/training.

  • Equity opportunities so you can share in our growth and success.

  • Unlimited PTO and flexibility when you need it the most.

Why Choose Alternative Payments?

title: Senior Software Engineer, Data Platform
description:
About Empyrean

Empyrean Solutions is the fastest growing financial risk management and performance solutions platform, specifically designed for banks and credit unions. Since 2008, we've been trusted by financial institutions across the globe to deliver cutting-edge ALM, budgeting, profitability analysis, and compliance tools through our unified Empyrean Dataverse® platform. Our solutions emphasize speed, accuracy, and ease of use to help financial institutions make faster, more informed decisions.

At Empyrean Solutions, you won't just have a seat at the table - you'll help build it. Every person here has a direct, visible impact on where we go next. You'll work alongside a genuinely collaborative team, backed by AI tools available to every employee from day one.

The role

The Data Platform will be the home of all Empyrean data. Some products already run on it, others are moving over now, and new products, including our AI and reporting products, will be built on it from the start. The services, interfaces and patterns you build now are the ones they'll all run on. Over the next two to three years, volume per customer grows from a few million rows a month to more than 100 million rows a day.

We're hiring a senior software engineer to build that platform the way you'd build any enterprise SaaS backend, with services that load each record exactly once, contracts that don't break the products downstream, and tenants that can't see each other's data. You don't need a data engineering background. You do need to have shipped and run production backend systems, and you need to care whether the data is correct.

You'll join a platform team of four to five engineers and test automation engineers, working with a data architect who sets platform direction.

The role is hybrid requiring three 3 days a week in our office in Cork, Ireland.

What you'll work on

  • Event-driven ingestion services. Build the services that bring customer data onto the platform, delivering exactly-once results over at-least-once delivery. You know how they behave when things fail: retries, redelivery, reordering and late changes.

  • Versioned contracts and APIs. Build the interfaces, shared SDKs and data feeds that Empyrean products, and later our customers, use to read platform data. Keep them versioned, tested in CI and safe to evolve, so a platform change never surprises a team downstream.

  • Correct, reproducible results. Build point-in-time history and exact decimal arithmetic into the platform's types, tests and interfaces, so every product gets them by default, and any result can be reproduced exactly as it was on any past date.

  • Scale without runaway cost. Grow services and storage by orders of magnitude while keeping queries fast and costs rising more slowly than volume. Measure first, and back changes with load tests and cost data.

  • Self-service onboarding. Build the control-plane services and tooling that bring a new product or a new customer onto the platform in days, not months, within our multi-tenant model.

  • Data ready for AI and ML. Make customer data usable by models and AI features, with the same contracts, tenant separation and reproducibility as everything else on the platform.

  • Operability built in. Ship SLOs, alerting and CI gates with every service, and take part in incident response for what you own. Each incident ends with a fix that stops it recurring.

What you bring

  • 5+ years building software professionally, including backend services you designed, deployed and ran in production. We care more about what you've built and operated than about the count.

  • Production experience in Python, C#/.NET, Java or a similar backend language. Our platform services are mostly Python, and our shared data SDK and the products that use it are .NET. We use AI tooling heavily, so if you come from Java or another language, you'll pick up Python and C# quickly.

  • Instincts for distributed systems: idempotency, ordering, concurrency, retries, and what "exactly once" costs.

  • Testing as a habit: unit tests, integration tests against real dependencies, and CI that fails when it should.

  • Experience evolving APIs and schemas: versioning, backward compatibility, and moving consumers over without a big-bang cutover.

  • Strong SQL, and a working understanding of how a cloud data warehouse executes and bills a query.

  • You understand how multi-tenant software keeps each customer's data separate, and you build within that model: scoped service identities, least-privilege access, and no shortcuts.

  • You mentor through code review and pairing, and you leave behind patterns and docs that others can follow without you.

  • You write clearly. You measure before you propose a design, and your PRs say what changed, why, how you tested it and what could go wrong.

Nice to have

  • Experience with systems where exact numbers and audit history matter, such as payments, billing, ledgers or accounting.

Our stack

Python and C#/.NET, Snowflake, dbt, Terraform, Azure (Functions, Container Apps, Service Bus), GitHub Actions. Beyond a strong backend language, you don't need experience with any of these. You'll pick them up here.

How we work

  • Small team, high autonomy. You know how your area is designed, built and run in production. Our data architect owns the overall platform direction, and you bring evidence to those decisions.

  • AI-first. Claude Code and Cursor are part of how we build. We expect you to use them well, and to review what they produce as hard as you review your own work.

  • Significant decisions go through written RFCs with measured evidence.

  • Someone other than the author verifies every change, and code reviews have substance.

This probably isn't the role for you if

  • Your production experience is mostly notebooks or scheduled SQL, with no service you've had to keep running.

  • You'd rather deduplicate in a downstream query than fix why the duplicates arrive.

  • You work best from fully specified tickets.

description:
Schuldhulpverlener Fase 1

Als Schuldhulpverlener Fase 1 ben je het eerste aanspreekpunt voor inwoners met financiële vragen, betalingsachterstanden of problematische schulden. Je brengt samen met de inwoner de financiële situatie en hulpvraag zorgvuldig in kaart en zorgt voor rust, overzicht en perspectief. Ook signalen vanuit vroegsignalering pak je op.

Je kijkt verder dan alleen de schulden en hebt oog voor andere leefgebieden die van invloed zijn op de financiële situatie. Samen met de inwoner bepaal je welke stappen nodig zijn en leg je deze vast in een plan van aanpak. Je voert hierop de regie, bewaakt de voortgang en werkt toe naar een passende en duurzame oplossing.

Wat je gaat doen:

  • Voeren van intakegesprekken met inwoners met financiële vragen, betalingsachterstanden of schulden;

  • Oppakken van signalen vanuit vroegsignalering;

  • Analyseren van de financiële situatie en de aard en ernst van de problematiek;

  • Geven van duidelijke informatie en passend advies over de mogelijkheden binnen schuldhulpverlening;

  • Samen met de inwoner opstellen van een plan van aanpak met concrete doelen en vervolgstappen;

  • Voeren van regie op het plan van aanpak en bewaken van afspraken en voortgang;

  • Voorbereiden van een minnelijke schuldregeling wanneer deze passend en haalbaar is;

  • Zorgdragen voor een goede overdracht naar de collega die de minnelijke schuldregeling volgens het 120-dagenmodel uitvoert;

  • Verzorgen van nazorg na afronding van een schuldregeling;

  • Ondersteunen van inwoners bij het behouden van financiële stabiliteit en het voorkomen van nieuwe schulden;

  • Samenwerken met collega’s binnen het Sociaal Team en verschillende ketenpartners;

  • Verbinden van verschillende expertises om tot een integrale en duurzame oplossing te komen.

  • Kennis van de Wet gemeentelijke schuldhulpverlening (Wgs) en het vakgebied schuldhulpverlening;

  • Je kunt snel de aard en ernst van financiële problematiek inschatten en jouw aanpak hierop afstemmen;

  • Je bent vaardig in onderhandelen en durft duidelijke grenzen te stellen;

  • Je neemt verantwoordelijkheid en durft beslissingen te nemen wanneer dit nodig is;

  • Je werkt integraal en zoekt actief de samenwerking met collega’s en ketenpartners.

De functie is voor 24 uur per week.

title: EPIC Early Childhood Services - LCSW or LMFT Clinical Supervisor
description:
ORGANIZATIONAL OVERVIEW

East Bay Agency for Children’s (EBAC) mission is to improve the well-being of children, youth, and families by reducing the impact of trauma and social inequities. EBAC strives to reduce barriers that contribute to disparities in wellness for socio-economically disadvantaged and racially marginalized families and to create communities where all children and families have support systems to reach their full potential.

EBAC was established in 1952 when a group of parents of children with autism wanted to give their children the same educational and recreational opportunities that contribute to the physical well-being and social growth of all children. From this was born the first day-treatment program west of the Mississippi and was the foundation of growth in meeting the needs of children and families living in the San Francisco Bay Area, and especially in Alameda County.

Today, EBAC’s programs serve over 10,000 children, youth and families throughout Alameda County each year with the goal of giving each child and family the specific resources, skills, and support they need to help them reach their full potential. The organization has strategically grown its program offerings to include a wide variety of supports and services to the community. For more information about our organization, please visit the website at www.ebac.org.

QUALIFICATIONS and COMPETENCY FACTORS

A. POSITION SUMMARY & FUNCTION

Role Overview

The Clinical Supervisor will provide vital leadership and clinical oversight to our EPIC Early Childhood Services Program. In this dynamic role, you will collaborate closely with internal teams and external community partners to strengthen our place-based continuum of care and drive positive, measurable outcomes for the populations we serve.

Our Clinical Framework

At EBAC, we are deeply committed to equity and healing. All of our clinical programs operate strictly through a social justice and trauma-informed lens, purposefully designed to support, uplift, and provide high-quality care to under-resourced and under-served communities.

Core Objectives of the Role

  • Provide Clinical Leadership: Deliver robust clinical supervision, mentorship, and guidance to program staff to ensure the highest standard of care.
  • Foster Collaboration: Build and maintain strong partnerships across internal departments and external community organizations to create a seamless, supportive network for clients.
  • Drive Community Impact: Support, evaluate, and enhance our place-based services to ensure interventions are effective, culturally responsive, and achieving positive community outcomes.

B. QUALIFICATIONS and COMPETENCY FACTORS

Required Credentials & Experience

  1. Licensure: Active LCSW or LMFT license, meeting all Board of Behavioral Sciences (BBS) criteria to act as a Clinical Supervisor in a mental health discipline (must include a minimum of two years post-licensure experience). Must have fully completed all BBS supervisor training requirements and be able to provide completion certificates at the time of hire/first day of work.
  2. Clinical Supervision: Demonstrated experience supervising pre-licensed interns or associates, specifically those providing child and family therapy within a community mental health setting.
  3. Quality Assurance: Proven experience in clinical chart auditing, Quality Assurance (QA) monitoring, and ensuring compliance with behavioral health standards.
  4. Technical Proficiency: Strong ability to efficiently navigate Electronic Health Record (EHR) platforms and web-based systems to review clinical documentation, track work performance, and manage records.
  5. Communication & Leadership: Exceptional supervisory, administrative, and interpersonal skills, with a strong capacity for clear written and verbal communication.
  6. Mobility: Valid driver’s license, active auto insurance, and access to a reliable vehicle for travel as needed.

title: PREA Advocate
description:
WEAVE’s mission is to promote safe and healthy relationships and support survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, and sex trafficking. WEAVE’s vision is When Everyone Acts, Violence Ends.


Job Description

The PREA Advocate provides trauma-informed advocacy, crisis intervention, forensic exam accompaniment, education, and support services to incarcerated individuals who experience sexual assault within Sacramento County detention and reentry facilities. This position serves youth at the Sacramento County Youth Detention Facility (YDF) and adult survivors participating in the Saint John's Program Female Community Reentry Program (SJFCRP).

The Advocate delivers individual and group support services, coordinates referrals and PREA reporting, provides accompaniment to forensic medical exams, and collaborates with facility staff to ensure survivors have access to confidential, victim-centered services. The position operates within correctional environments and requires the ability to build collaborative relationships with detention staff while maintaining victim autonomy, confidentiality, and a trauma-informed approach.

Advocacy Services

  • Provide crisis intervention and emotional support to incarcerated individuals who experience sexual abuse within detention and correctional settings in Sacramento County.
  • Conduct individual advocacy sessions utilizing a trauma-informed, victim-centered approach.
  • Facilitate peer support groups and educational activities addressing sexual violence, healing, coping skills, and available resources.
  • Respond to requests for services from victims, facility personnel, and partner agencies.
  • Provide follow-up support as requested by survivors.
  • Advocate on behalf of survivors regarding issues related to sexual assault within the facility, consistent with facility policies and victim authorization.
  • Support victims in navigating institutional systems and understanding available options.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary partners to address barriers impacting survivor safety and well-being.

Accompaniment Services

  • Provide accompaniment and support during forensic medical examinations, interviews, hearings, court proceedings, and other appointments related to sexual assault within a facility.
  • Coordinate accompaniment services in accordance with detention facility and community reentry program protocols.
  • Maintain knowledge of forensic examination procedures and correctional protocols relevant to incarcerated survivors.

Outreach, Education, and Training

  • Develop and maintain positive working relationships with detention facility and reentry program personnel.
  • Provide education regarding sexual assault services available to incarcerated survivors.
  • Distribute informational and outreach materials throughout the facility.
  • Conduct presentations, support groups, educational workshops, and awareness-building activities.

Case Documentation and Program Administration

  • Maintain accurate, timely, and confidential client and program records using WEAVE’s confidential services database.
  • Document services provided in accordance with agency, grant, and regulatory requirements.
  • Assist with grant reporting requirements and program evaluation activities.
  • Participate in agency meetings, training, and professional development opportunities.


Collaboration and Partnership Responsibilities

  • Serve as a liaison between WEAVE, Sacramento County Youth Detention Facility, Saint John's Program Female Community Reentry Program, and other facilities in Sacramento County.
  • Foster positive partnerships that increase survivor access to services within detention settings.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and comply with all facility policies and procedures.
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • Associate degree in social work, behavioral health, human services, or a related field, or equivalent relevant education, training, and/or experience. .
  • Understanding of, or ability to learn, systems affecting incarcerated youth and adults, including juvenile justice, detention, corrections, and reentry systems.
  • Ability to establish rapport with diverse populations, including criminal justice-involved individuals.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries.
  • Strong crisis intervention and de-escalation skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to facilitate educational presentations and support groups.
  • Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.
  • Strong organizational and documentation skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with internal and external partners.
  • Complete WEAVE’s 69-hour peer counselor training program and pass background check (post-hiring requirement).
  • Annual completion of WEAVE’s continuing education requirements to maintain Peer Counselor Certification.
  • Ability to travel reliably between assigned work locations throughout Sacramento County. A valid driver's license and proof of insurance are required when driving on WEAVE business.

WEAVE is committed to providing inclusive, accessible, and respectful workplaces for all staff, including those with disabilities such as being in a wheelchair, Deaf or Hard of Hearing, blind or low vision or other access or functional needs and we works to equip staff of all abilities with reasonable accommodation to perform their job functions. These can include the provision of adaptive equipment, materials in alternate formats, and flexible work schedules. Our priority is to provide ongoing, individualized accommodation to give all staff access to resources best suited to their needs. Work environment is primarily a busy office setting in a two-story building with stairs and an elevator, or in various community settings to deliver training/presentations. title: Client Service Monitor - FT
description:
Hope Mission Statement

The mission of Hope the Mission is to prevent, reduce and eliminate poverty, hunger, and homelessness by offering immediate assistance and long-term solutions.

Position Purpose and Summary

The Client Services Monitor (CSM) works directly on-site and is responsible for keeping participants safe, supporting daily operations, community standards and helping Hope the Mission's Interim Housing programs run smoothly. The CSM plays an important role in creating an environment that is safe, structured, and respectful — one where every participant is treated with dignity and fairness.

This position requires someone who shows up consistently, uses good judgment, and genuinely cares about serving people experiencing homelessness. Many participants in our programs have been through long periods of instability, crisis, and trauma. When a CSM shows up with calm, care, and compassion, it creates a sense of safety and routine that participants can count on as they work toward stable housing.

The CSM reports to the Program Manager or Assistant Program Manager and works alongside site staff to make sure the program runs well, meets contract requirements, and reflects Hope the Mission's values in every interaction.


Primary Duties and Responsibilities

Facility Maintenance and Sanitation

  • Assists with and facilitates routine cleaning of all facility areas to maintain cleanliness, safety, and operational readiness

  • Cleans and disinfects restrooms and shower areas after each use, without exception. Maintains sanitary and safe restroom and sink conditions at all times. Completes deep cleaning of restrooms and common areas.

  • Monitors and maintains hygiene areas and community areas; ensures resources are fully stocked, replenishing as needed.

  • Washes, dries, and prepares towels used for restroom and shower services

  • Monitors laundry rooms, restrooms, and common areas to ensure cleanliness and appropriate use

  • Maintains accurate shower and restroom usage logs

Participant Safety and Monitoring

  • Conducts required wellness checks each shift to ensure participant safety and well-being

  • Monitors participant movement, common areas, and site activity to promote safety and program compliance

  • Conducts routine site walk-throughs and safety checks during assigned shifts

  • Supports contraband control and safety procedures in accordance with agency policy

  • Responds to incidents and emergencies using trauma-informed de-escalation techniques and follows all incident reporting protocols

  • Supports emergency responses — including medical emergencies, overdoses, and evacuations — until leadership or first responders arrive

Participant Services and Engagement

  • Provides direct, respectful assistance to participants, including answering questions, responding to requests, and connecting participants to appropriate staff or resources

  • Assists with participant intake, orientation, and explanation of site guidelines as directed by management

  • Distributes hygiene supplies including soap, shampoo, towels, and related items to participants as needed

  • Supports meal service, supply distribution, and general operational duties as assigned

Documentation and Reporting

  • Completes Daily Activity Reports (DARs) accurately, objectively, and in a timely manner

  • Conducts intake, exit, and case notes in HMIS where applicable

  • Assists with documentation related to participant movements, wellness concerns, or incidents as required

  • Observes and reports safety concerns, maintenance issues, guideline violations, and unusual occurrences to site leadership promptly

Shift Operations

  • Provides support during shift pass-downs and communicates relevant updates between shifts

  • Provides overnight, evening, weekend, or holiday coverage as scheduled

  • Performs other duties as assigned

Transportation (Site Specific)

  • Transports participants to and from established routes and as directed by a supervisor

  • Maintains vehicle cleanliness inside and out at all times

  • Ensures the vehicle has sufficient fuel before and during each shift

  • Completes daily vehicle maintenance checks and reports any issues to the supervisors

  • Logs all mileage accurately and in accordance with departmental procedures

Skills

  • Strong observation and situational awareness skills

  • Trauma-informed communication and de-escalation techniques

  • Ability to maintain professional boundaries with participants

  • Clear, objective, and professional written documentation skills

  • Ability to follow policies, procedures, and chain of command

  • Strong teamwork and communication skills

  • Basic computer and email proficiency

  • Ability to lead with integrity and uphold organizational mission, values, and service philosophy.

  • Ability to cultivate and maintain collaborative relationships with community-based organizations and external service providers. Strong Interpersonal Skills.

  • Maintains professionalism, empathy, and sound decision-making when working in complex or emotionally challenging environments.


Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required

  • Previous experience in homeless services, shelter operations or social service preferred

  • Knowledge of trauma-informed care and harm reduction principles preferred

  • Ability to work flexible schedules including nights, weekends, and holidays


Mandatory Requirements

  • Background Screening – Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of background checks as required per worksite.

  • Drug and Alcohol Testing – Candidates must pass pre-employment and ongoing drug and alcohol screenings in accordance with company policy.

  • Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) Check – For roles requiring driving, employment is contingent upon an acceptable driving record.

  • Legal Eligibility to Work – Candidates must provide proof of legal authorization to work in the US.

  • Compliance with Company Policies and HIPAA standards – All employees must comply with company policies, including safety, confidentiality, and conduct standards.


Physical, Demands, Environmental Conditions, Equipment

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions. The employee is required to: walk and climb stairs; stand, bend, squat, climb, kneel, and twist on an intermittent or sometimes continuous basis; grasp, push, pull objects such as files, file cabinet drawers, and reach overhead; handle, finger, grasp and feel objects and equipment; reach with hands and arms; be mobile by moving oneself from place to place quickly and easily; repeat various motions with the wrists, hands, and fingers; be able to perform visual activities for (including, but not limited to) administrative and clerical tasks; ability to lift up to 25 lbs.; communicate, receive and exchange ideas, information by means of the spoken and written word; drive vehicles in and around Los Angeles County; be able to enter various buildings that may require climbing stairs; be periodically subjected to outside environmental conditions. The employee may work in proximity to service animals and emotional support animals; use a desktop and/or laptop computer; various office machines. Complete all required forms in personal writing.


Work Environment

The employee may be in contact with individuals and families in crisis who may be ill, using alcohol and drugs, and who may not be attentive to basic personal hygiene, health and safety practices. The employee may experience a number of unpleasant sensory demands associated with the participants’ use of alcohol and drugs, and lack of personal hygiene. The employee must be ready to respond quickly and effectively to many types of situations, including crisis situations and potentially hostile situations. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate in an office setting. Sometimes work may become stressful when working under pressure or in crisis intervention. .

The WSBA's mission is to serve the public and the members of the Bar, to ensure the integrity of the legal profession, and to champion justice.

The Intake Disciplinary Counsel reviews, investigates, and analyzes a high volume of grievances against lawyers; prepares dismissal letters and legal memos; and supports the Managing Disciplinary Counsel – Intake by making determinations on opening case files, grievance disposition, developing Intake processes and procedures, and guiding nonlawyer staff on how to respond to inquiries from members and the public about the lawyer discipline system.

title: Category Specialist: Engineering
description:

The Category Specialist: Engineering supports the development and execution of category strategies for engineering-related goods, services, projects, maintenance requirements, and technical solutions across AECI operations.

The role is responsible for supporting strategic sourcing activities, supplier relationship management, market intelligence gathering, contract administration, spend analysis, and value delivery initiatives within the Engineering category portfolio.

Working closely with Engineering, Maintenance, Operations, Projects, Supply Chain, SHEQ, Commercial and Finance stakeholders, the incumbent contributes to delivering cost-effective, safe, reliable and sustainable supply solutions that support operational excellence, plant reliability and business growth objectives.

The role supports key categories including:

  • Maintenance, Repair and Operations (MRO) supplies
  • Mechanical equipment
  • Electrical equipment
  • Instrumentation and control systems
  • Capital project procurement
  • Technical and consulting services
  • Fabrication and construction services
  • Reliability and condition-monitoring services

Key Accountabilities

Development of sourcing strategies

  • Support the development of strategic sourcing approaches for critical mechanical equipment, engineering spares and maintenance services to improve plant reliability and operational continuity
  • Manage sourcing activities for engineering spares, maintenance services and operational requirements
  • Drive end-to-end sourcing activities, including RFx processes, supplier evaluations, commercial negotiations, and supplier selection.
  • Support the development and continuous refinement of category strategies through market intelligence and demand insights.
  • Conduct ongoing spend analysis, market and supplier research to identify opportunities, risks, and alternative supply sources.
  • Continuously monitor supplier markets, risks and availability to support operational continuity
  • Identify alternative suppliers and sourcing opportunities to improve reliability and responsiveness
  • Provide input into Procurement dashboards and tracking tools.
  • Support procurement planning through spend analysis, demand forecasting and supplier insights
  • Contribute to budgeting and forecasting processes through spend and cost analysis.
  • Proactively identify and mitigate supply and commercial risks within assigned categories.
  • Ensure procurement activities align with operational, maintenance and shutdown requirements

Cost Optimisation and Value Delivery

  • Conduct detailed spend analysis across managed categories to identify cost-saving opportunities, demand drivers, and initiatives to reduce operational inefficiencies and procurement lead times. Identify, develop, and implement cost-saving and value-creation initiatives aligned to procurement targets
  • Support the implementation of category-led initiatives, to ensure value delivery and in line with procurement targets
  • Apply total cost of ownership (TCO) principles to enable optimal sourcing decisions
  • Perform cost modelling, scenario analysis, and should-cost modelling using market and supplier data.
  • Support standardisation and optimisation initiatives across engineering and maintenance procurement
  • Track and report on savings delivery and benefits realisation
  • Support optimisation of engineering inventory and critical spare holdings to balance operational reliability and working capital requirements
  • Identify opportunities to reduce emergency procurement through improved planning, supplier alignment and sourcing strategies
  • Drive standardisation initiatives across engineering and maintenance categories to reduce complexity and improve procurement efficiency
  • Build and maintain a qualified supplier base for assigned categories
  • Manage supplier performance across quality, cost, service delivery and responsiveness
  • Support supplier segmentation and contribute to supplier category and/ or diversification strategies
  • Monitor supplier performance through defined KPIs (cost, quality, delivery, service, sustainability) and drive continuous improvement initiatives
  • Lead supplier performance reviews and implement corrective actions where required
  • Develop and maintain strategic relationships with OEMs and specialised engineering suppliers to improve technical support, responsiveness and lifecycle value
  • Drive supplier innovation and continuous improvement

Stakeholder engagement and collaboration

  • Partner with internal stakeholders (Operations, Commercial, Finance, S&OP, R&D) to support plant reliability and operational continuity
  • Support shutdown and turnaround planning through sourcing readiness, supplier coordination and critical spares availability
  • Provide procurement support and commercial guidance on engineering and CAPEX requirements
  • Contribute to S&OP processes and support demand planning inputs for key suppliers
  • Provide data-driven insights and recommendations to support business needs
  • Continuously ensure alignment between procurement activities and operational requirements
  • Support budgeting processes through accurate spend and cost analysis
  • Act as a trusted advisor to stakeholders on sourcing and supplier-related matters on managed categories
  • Champion all procurement improvement programs / initiatives E.g. Digitisation, Policy Rollout

Contracts management

  • Develop and execute negotiations strategies for new and existing suppliers to achieve optimal commercial outcomes and lowest total cost of ownership, and meet savings targets
  • Lead commercial negotiations within delegated authority to achieve optimal pricing and contractual outcomes
  • Support the drafting, review, and management of contracts, ensuring alignment with business requirements and risk mitigation principles
  • Monitor contract compliance and utilisation, identifying risks and improvement opportunities
  • Ensure all procurement activities comply with internal governance frameworks and policies

KPI’s

  • Percentage of spend under contract
  • Cost savings and value delivery against targets
  • Compliance to negotiated agreements
  • Compliance to procurement policies and approved vendor lists
  • Supplier scorecard performance (quality, OTIF, cost, sustainability)
  • Engineering spares and service availability and supply continuity
  • Timely completion of sourcing initiatives
  • Successful support of project procurement milestones
  • Risk mitigation effectiveness across key categories
  • BBBEE and supplier development impact
  • Reduction in engineering procurement lead times
  • Enable plant reliability through strategic sourcing of engineering spares and services and supplier performance

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Procurement or related discipline
  • Postgraduate qualification in Procurement, Supply Chain or Business Management – advantageous
  • Professional procurement certification (for example CIPS) – advantageous
  • Project Management certification (PMP, Prince2 or equivalent) – advantageous

Experience Required

  • Minimum of 5 years proven experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, engineering procurement, supply chain or operations
  • Experience within manufacturing, industrial chemicals, engineering or maintenance environments
  • Proven experience managing engineering spares, maintenance services, CAPEX procurement and mechanical equipment sourcing
  • Experience in supplier negotiations, contract management and sourcing strategy development
  • Exposure to SAP ERP systems and eProcurement platforms (Coupa advantageous)
  • Experience working in cross-functional operational environments
  • Demonstrated capability to operate in a multi-regional environment, ensuring alignment, consistency, and effective stakeholder engagement.

Skills

  • Strong communication, leadership and people management capability.
  • Strategic sourcing and category management
  • Engineering and mechanical procurement management
  • Supplier negotiation and contract management
  • Cost modelling and Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) application
  • Spend analysis and procurement reporting
  • Stakeholder engagement and influencing capability
  • Project and execution management
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability

Knowledge

  • Mechanical equipment and industrial services sourcing
  • Procurement governance and compliance frameworks
  • Operational and plant maintenance requirements
  • ERP systems (SAP preferred) and procurement platforms
  • Market analysis and commercial evaluation techniques

Behaviours

  • Strategic thinker with strong problem-solving ability
  • Results-driven with strong commercial acumen
  • Operationally focused and solution-oriented
  • Collaborative and relationship-focused
  • High attention to detail and governance orientation

description:
About Us

The Michigan Milk Producers Association (MMPA) is a member-owned and operated milk marketing cooperative known for producing high-quality, award-winning dairy products. Established in 1916, MMPA markets 5 billion pounds of milk annually and is the ninth largest dairy farmer-owned cooperative in the United States, serving members in Michigan, Ohio, Indiana and Wisconsin. At MMPA, commitment to milk quality begins on the farm and extends through five processing facilities and wholly owned subsidiary brands, Superior Dairy and Heritage Ridge Creamery. With seven sites across Michigan, Indiana and Ohio, MMPA continues to shape the future of the dairy industry through innovation, product diversification and strategic growth while returning value to its member-owners.

Why you’ll love working here

  • Competitive salary
  • Health and wellness benefits with medical coverage through Blue Cross Blue Shield, including mental health benefits
  • Disability insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Retirement including 401k with employer contributions
  • Personal and professional growth opportunities
  • Employee appreciation events and recognition awards
  • Employee wellness initiatives
  • Employee feedback and suggestion forums

Position Summary

The Michigan Milk Producers Association is looking for an experienced CMMS Administrator to join our team in our Constantine, MI facility. The CMMS Administrator will play a crucial role in the implementation of a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) at the facility. This position will be responsible for collecting asset information, preventive maintenance data from OEMs, and setting up the R&M inventory within the CMMS.

The CMMS Administrator will work collaboratively with various stakeholders to ensure the successful integration of the system, enhance maintenance efficiency, and support operational excellence.

Job Responsibilities

  • Support the implementation of the CMMS, including system configuration, data migration, and user training.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to identify and define system requirements and processes.
  • Collect and organize asset information, including specifications, maintenance history, and operational data.
  • Gather preventive maintenance (PM) schedules and procedures from OEMs and internal sources.
  • Set up and categorize inventory, including spare parts and consumables, within the CMMS.
  • Develop training materials and conduct training sessions to ensure effective utilization of the CMMS.
  • Provide ongoing support and troubleshooting assistance for CMMS users.
  • Work closely with Plant Engineers, Maintenance Managers, and project teams to align maintenance strategies and practices.
  • Facilitate communication and collaboration across departments to promote reliability and continuous improvement.
  • Monitor CMMS performance and user engagement, providing regular updates to management.
  • Generate reports on maintenance metrics, asset performance, and inventory levels to support decision-making.
  • Partner with the Maintenance Manager to identify opportunities for process improvements and system enhancements.
  • Optimize preventive maintenance schedules to align with production requirements and minimize downtime.
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement by encouraging feedback and innovation from maintenance staff and operators.
  • Stay current on industry best practices, technological advancements, and emerging trends in maintenance management.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Finance, Supply Chain, Mathematics, or a related discipline preferred
  • Experience in purchasing, inventory control, and maintenance planning within a manufacturing or industrial environment
  • CMMS implementation or administration experience preferred (examples include Maximo, PMC, PMX, SAP PM, or similar systems)
  • Strong understanding of maintenance management principles, preventive maintenance practices, and asset management
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and experience with data analysis tools
  • Excellent organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate across departments
  • Strong research and technical writing skills, including documentation, instructions, and presentations
  • Six Sigma training or certification is strongly preferred

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to work in a manufacturing environment, including exposure to noise, temperature fluctuations, and mechanical hazards
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds and perform tasks requiring manual dexterity
  • Perform other duties as assigned

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each responsibility satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the responsibilities.

title: Software Engineer
description:
High performance isn't a given. It’s built on standards.

Standards that have driven McLaren for over 60 years.

And if you’re ready for the challenge, that standard is yours to own.

Burning enthusiasm. Constant improvement. The thrill in the pursuit of better.

That’s how we build a legacy. And how you build a career here.

Because racing isn’t just something we do. It’s who we are.

We are racers.

Are you?

Job Description

Join the dual-series software team supporting McLaren’s Hypercar and IndyCar teams. You will help develop and support high-quality, bespoke software tools that enable our engineering teams to analyse data, improve performance and deliver results on track.

This is an opportunity to contribute to two events within the Triple Crown of Motorsport: the Indianapolis 500-Mile Race and the 24 Heures du Mans. You will work within a close-knit team where everyone takes accountability, continuously improves and plays a vital role in our on-track success.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Contribute to the development of bespoke software solutions used to analyse data, improve performance and deliver results on track.
  • Work across multiple projects involving a wide range of programming languages, technologies and data formats.
  • Participate in the complete software lifecycle, including requirements analysis, specification, architecture and design, development, deployment, maintenance and support.
  • Support the software and tools produced by the team, collaborating daily with engineers across the IndyCar and Hypercar engineering organisations.
  • Respond to support queries and alerts, check monitoring and systems, and help maintain the smooth day-to-day operation of the team.
  • Contribute to stand-up, retrospective and planning meetings.
  • Continue developing your professional skills and identify new tools and technologies that could benefit the team.
  • Provide event support across different time zones, including frequent out-of-hours and weekend working.
  • Occasionally provide trackside support and travel internationally.
  • Take on additional responsibilities suited to your skills when required to help the team go racing.

Qualifications

  • At least two years of commercial experience applying software engineering in a practical environment.
  • Motorsport experience or equivalent experience within a fast-paced, high-performance environment, such as the military, games or aerospace industries, real-time systems or a similar setting.
  • A strong theoretical understanding of object-oriented programming, design patterns and principles, data structures and algorithms, relational and NoSQL databases, and test-driven development.
  • A BSc in Computer Science or a relevant engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • High proficiency in at least one common programming language used in a commercial environment, such as C# or Python.
  • Some experience with HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
  • Familiarity with technologies such as Kubernetes is preferred.
  • The adaptability to work with different technologies according to engineering requirements.
  • A collaborative, small-team mentality and the determination to deliver high-quality work on time.
  • The ability to work effectively with engineers and technicians from a range of disciplines.

The team is based at the McLaren Technology Centre in Woking and operates a flexible hybrid model, with regular office-based collaboration.

Additional Information

Success in racing comes from bringing together talented people with different skills, perspectives and experiences. We're committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone feels supported and empowered to deliver their best work.

Every role has the potential to drive high performance. You'll be part of a team united by a shared ambition to push boundaries and embody our racing mindset. We invest in our people through opportunities to develop and grow, creating an environment where individuals and teams can thrive.

Alongside a range of wellbeing initiatives and development opportunities, we're committed to helping you build a rewarding career and make your mark at McLaren Racing.

As a 24/7 operation, we have openings across all shifts, including days, evenings, weekends, and 12-hour schedules. Candidates must be flexible and willing to work any shift based on operational needs. Some schedules may qualify for shift differential. Overtime—both scheduled and unscheduled, including holidays—may also be required.

DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Research technical data and performs inspection of hangered aircraft in heavy maintenance checks, of flightline/storage induction or reactivation and back shop repair/overhaul maintenance activities in accordance with applicable aircraft/component maintenance manuals, FAA regulations and Ascent Aviation policies and procedures.
  • Enforces Quality Control standards for material receiving, shipping, storage, handling, repairs and overhaul to see that quality, allowable tolerances and other specifications and standards set by the Ascent Aviation and the applicable manufacturer are met.
  • Performs inspection of aircraft components during their assembly, installation and adjustment phases of incorporation onto an aircraft to ensure that the workmanship and materials conform to the aircraft manufacturers specifications and maintenance manual procedures.
  • Ensures that all Work-In-Progress is properly documented as to the worked performed and that corrective actions used, have the proper technical data references documented properly in the corrective action block and the work in progress steps.
  • Records all inspection data on the proper form, report and/or inspection tag and bring to the attention of the Lead Inspector any irregularities in the daily standard practices used that would cause injury to personnel or the aircraft unsafe or unairworthy.
  • Performs maintenance work/repair of company equipment and general shop housecleaning.
  • Tests tightness of airframe connections with hand tools and utilizes flashlight and mirror to inspect fit of parts.
  • Examines assembly, installation, and adjustment of ailerons and rudders to ensure that workmanship and materials conform with Civil Air Regulations, company specifications, and manual procedures.
  • Determines accuracy of installation of components in power plant and hydraulic system using protractor, micrometer, calipers, and gauges to ensure that specified tolerances are met.
  • Signs inspection tag to approve unit, or records reasons for rejecting unit.
  • Logs inspections performed on aircraft.
  • Ensure that all work performed is done in a safe manner. Directs activities to protect employees from harm and maintain safe working conditions.
  • Performs facility audits for safety and policy compliance.
  • Coordinates with customer representatives.
  • Performs duties of Lead Inspector in his/her absence.
  • Ensures that proper documentation is made on training record for training received, and signed by Lead, Supervisor, or Manager.
  • Performs maintenance duties away from base on temporary duty.

YOU WILL GET MORE THAN JUST COMPENSATION:

  • 401K with company match
  • Medical/Dental/Vision Insurance
  • PTO – Eligible for up to 3 weeks in your first year, in addition to 7 paid company holidays
  • Company provided Life Insurance
  • Development and Career Growth Opportunities

REQUIRED SKILLS/ABILITIES:

  • Strong organizational and planning skills with the ability to meet deadlines
  • High attention to detail and accuracy
  • Proficiency in reading, writing, and understanding the English language
  • Skilled in using computer systems, maintenance manuals, documentation systems, and applying Federal Aviation Regulations

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Minimum Requirements:

  • A&P License (valid and current)
  • 1 year of aircraft maintenance experience in a Part 145 Repair Station
    OR 5 years as a licensed A&P in a similar aviation operation

Preferred Requirements:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 2+ years of inspection experience in a high-volume MRO environment

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods of time.
  • Frequent bending, stooping, squatting, crouching, kneeling, balancing, and reaching above shoulder level.
  • Occasional crawling, climbing, lifting, carrying, pushing, or pulling up to 50 lbs. unassisted.
  • Requires eye-hand coordination and manual dexterity.
  • Corrected vision and hearing to normal range.

EQUIPMENT OPERATED:

  • Protective equipment required: Goggles, safety glasses, face shields, ear protection, apron, gloves, safety harness, breathing equipment.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

  • The work location will include aircraft Maintenance hangars, the flightline, and Avionics shop.
  • Potential hazards include exposure to high intensity noise levels, extreme changes in temperature, electrical charges and radar waves, materials identified on the Safety Data Sheets, and working around moving machinery.

OTHER DUTIES:

  • May be required to work at both Marana, AZ and Tucson, AZ locations as business needs dictate.
  • Additional duties may be assigned at the discretion of department management.

SMS REQUIREMENTS:

  • Employees are responsible for performing their duties in accordance with company policies and government regulations. These rules are written in the interest of preserving the lives and the resources entrusted to each employee, and when the rules are violated, the risk of a mishap is usually increased.
  • Employees shall participate in safety education programs and train to recognize hazards on the job and how to report them promptly. As a condition of employment, each member of Ascent Aviation agrees to report errors, incidents, and accidents honestly.
  • An employee who observes an unsafe action or condition should bring it to the attention of supervisors and managers. Certain conditions may allow the employee to easily correct or condition a situation.

Duties not listed within the position description may be required of the employee at the discretion of the department management. Job functions may vary due to irregular working conditions or multiple shift positions.

title: Pre-Certification Coordinator
description:
Job Description

Job Title: Pre-Certification Coordinator

Department: Revenue Cycle - Billing

Reports To: Revenue Cycle Manager

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

Approval Date: June 17, 2026


Summary

The Pre-Certification Coordinator supports the operational and authorization functions of the Revenue Cycle department. This role is responsible for obtaining prior authorizations, verifying insurance benefits, coordinating payer requirements, and maintaining accurate documentation to ensure timely reimbursement and continuity of patient care. The Coordinator partners with patients, providers, insurance carriers, and internal departments to ensure efficient workflows, regulatory compliance, and accurate claim processing.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Obtain and verify prior authorizations, precertifications, and treatment approvals for medical consultations, procedures, diagnostic testing, and elective services.
  • Verify insurance eligibility, benefits, provider participation status, coordination of benefits, and coverage requirements prior to service delivery.
  • Review payer requirements and analyze insurance information to determine authorization and reimbursement requirements.
  • Ensure all authorization requests are submitted accurately and within established departmental turnaround times.
  • Communicate authorization status updates, approvals, denials, and pending requests to clinical teams and appropriate departments in a timely manner.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of authorization activities, payer communications, and supporting records within the practice management system.
  • Monitor pending authorization requests and perform follow-up with insurance carriers to minimize delays in patient care and reimbursement.
  • Research and resolve authorization-related issues, documentation discrepancies, and payer inquiries.
  • Collaborate with Scheduling, Clinical, Billing, Front Desk, and Revenue Cycle teams to resolve workflow issues and improve operational efficiency.
  • Ensure compliance with HIPAA, CMS guidelines, payer regulations, and organizational policies and procedures.
  • Participate in departmental meetings, audits, training activities, and process improvement initiatives as assigned.
  • Other duties as assigned.


Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate’s degree preferred.
  • Minimum 3 years of healthcare, medical office, insurance verification, authorization, or revenue cycle experience required.
  • Knowledge of ICD-10, CPT, HCPCS coding, insurance authorization processes, coordination of benefits, and healthcare reimbursement practices preferred.
  • Experience with Athena, electronic medical records, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and healthcare practice management systems preferred.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, communication, customer service, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment while maintaining attention to detail and operational accuracy.


Supervisory Responsibilities

This job has no supervisory responsibilities.


Certificates, Licenses, Registrations

None required.


Physical Demands & Work Environment

Primarily office-based role requiring prolonged computer use, regular communication, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Occasional lifting up to 30 pounds may be required.

Job Summary

Leveraging a thorough understanding of the business data requirements & own data subject matter expertise (ahead of trend), set data architecture direction & lead the agile solution design, deployment, implementation & ongoing optimization of enterprise wide data retrieval, storage and distribution across an estate.

Job Description

Data Architecture & Data Engineering: Take ‘one stop shop’ accountability for the retrieval, storage, processing & distribution of data across a business area (data eco-system) Collaborate with data science teams & broader business & technical stakeholders to analyse customer data requirements & leverage analysis to identify & accurately spec / frame & set the appropriate data architecture for the business area Take accountability for deeply understanding the technical landscape and bank wide architecture that is connected to or dependent on the business area supported in order to effectively design & deliver data solutions (architecture, pipeline etc.) Leverage expertise in analytical & creative problem solving to synthesise data solution designs (build a solution from its components) beyond the analysis of the problem Lead design thinking processes to successfully deliver data solution blueprints & associated roadmaps Leverage state of the art relational and No-SQL databases as well integration and streaming platforms do deliver sustainable business specific data solutions. Lead the end to end solution design & implementation process for all data retrieval, storage & distribution solutions including contributing to and in some cases lead all phases of the development lifecycle including e.g. design process Develop high quality data retrieval, storage & distribution design and architecture in a test driven & domain driven / cross domain environment Build analytics tools that utilize the data pipeline by quickly producing well-organised, optimized, and documented source code & algorithms to deliver technical data solutions Create & Maintain Sophisticated CI / CD Pipelines (authoring & supporting CI/CD pipelines in Jenkins or similar tools and deploy to multisite environments – supporting and managing your applications all the way to production) Automate tasks through appropriate tools and scripting technologies e.g. Ansible, Chef Debug existing source code and polish feature sets. Assemble large, complex data sets that meet business requirements & manage the data pipeline Build infrastructure to automate extremely high volumes of data delivery and Creatively solve data volume and scaling challenges. Create data tools for analytics and data science teams that assist them in building and optimizing data sets for the benefit of the business Ensure designs & solutions support the technical organisation principles of self-service, repeatability, testability, scalability & resilience Apply general design patterns and paradigms to deliver technical solutions Inform & support the infrastructure build required for optimal extraction, transformation, and loading of data from a wide variety of data sources. Continuously optimise, improve & automate data retrieval, storage & distribution processes Work across the value chain and in particular with QA & CSO to define and implement quality assurance routines & processes Work across the value chain and in particular with QA & CSO to ensure the undisputable separation, security & quality of the organisation’s data Meaningfully contribute & ensure solutions align to the design & direction of the Group Architecture & in particular data standards, principles, preferences & practices. Short term deployment must align to strategic long-term delivery. Meaningfully contribute & ensure solutions align to the design and direction of the Group Infrastructure standards and practices e.g. OLA’s, IAAS, PAAS, SAAS, Containerisation etc. Strategically & operationally monitor the performance of data products and services ensuring ongoing optimization & cost to value for our businesses (think bank wide) Stay ahead of the curve on data retrieval, storage & distribution technologies & processes (global best practices & trends) to ensure best practice.

People Management:

title: Sr Software Engineer
description:
Job Requisition ID:


Location: Trinity Central, 152-160 Pearse St., Dublin 2.


Our city centre offices are right beside the back entrance to Pearse St Dart station. We’re super close to all major transport links, coffee shops/restaurants/gyms and minutes from Stephen’s Green and the city centre. However maybe the coffee and food is great at home and your commute is across the landing - we also offer a hybrid approach.


The role:


At HMH we’re a learning company. Our learning platforms serve millions of learners and educators.


We have interesting problems to solve, including how students interact with content from our learning platforms, how it impacts learning outcomes, and how to provide data driven guidance to maximize learner’s potential.


How we use data is at the heart of driving great learning experiences.


About the team you’re joining:


You’ll join the HMH data engineering team – here we get data into our Enterprise Data Lake and Enterprise Data Warehouse, and perform interesting data modelling. You’ll be helping to build a data platform and using it to analyse datasets and how they relate to each other to help answer customer’s questions.


You’ll be taking data from different sources, using big data tools to build data pipelines to serve our customer’s needs. We have many different consumers of our data, from data scientists to BI analysts to APIs. As a small and focused team, there’s a lot of flexibility, we give you the opportunity to work across many areas, to hone your data skills to where your passions lie.


More specifically you’ll be:



  • Helping our customers gain the most business value from our data platform by analysing, understanding and documenting our data lake and data warehouse datasets and supporting customers to empower them to answer their own questions

  • Leading in the design and implementation of data pipelines to populate our Enterprise Data Lake and Enterprise Data Warehouse using tools such as PySpark on AWS Glue, kafka connect, kinesis firehose.

  • Working independently on major system components.

  • Improving data infrastructure on AWS using deployment tools such as terraform, concourse.

  • Working closely with our data science, learning science and product teams to develop our data analytics capabilities, curate datasets and build out valuable business intelligence dashboards.

  • Architecting solutions for our customer’s problems and liaising with our Architecture function to get these solutions approved and implemented.

  • Automating and improving our internal processes.

  • Mentoring and coaching more junior members of the team.

  • Continuously looking to improve. We want you to seek out and actively apply best practice. We empower you to bring your ideas to the table and take a fresh look to help us continually improve technology practices, standards and methodologies.


Knowledge & Experience



  • ETL or data processing and orchestration experience.

  • Experience in python, java – spring boot would be beneficial.

  • AWS stack experience on a variety of the following services – VPC, Glue, s3, Lambda, Lake Formation, Athena, IAM.

  • Experience in CI/CD tooling and terraform.

  • Experience in SQL and working with relational databases.

  • Kubernetes experience would be beneficial but not essential.


ABOUT US


Houghton Mifflin Harcourt (NASDAQ:HMHC) is a global learning company dedicated to changing people’s lives by fostering passionate, curious learners. As a leading provider of pre-K-12 education content, services, and cutting-edge technology solutions across a variety of media, HMH enables learning in a changing landscape. HMH is uniquely positioned to create engaging and effective educational content and experiences from early childhood to beyond the classroom. HMH serves more than 50 million students in over 150 countries worldwide, while its award-winning children's books, novels, non-fiction, and reference titles are enjoyed by readers throughout the world.


For more information, visit http://careers.hmhco.com


Houghton Mifflin Harcourt is committed to a comprehensive policy of Equal Opportunities and we aim to create a workplace which provides for equal opportunities for all employees and potential employees.


Join us in transforming the educational experience!

  • Partner with the sourcing team to identify and evaluate new data procurement opportunities

The base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Hudson River Trading (HRT) brings a scientific approach to trading financial products. We have built one of the world's most sophisticated computing environments for research and development. Our researchers are at the forefront of innovation in the world of algorithmic trading.

At HRT we welcome a variety of expertise: mathematics and computer science, physics and engineering, media and tech. We’re a community of self-starters who are motivated by the excitement of being at the cutting edge of automation in every part of our organization—from trading, to business operations, to recruiting and beyond. We value openness and transparency, and celebrate great ideas from HRT veterans and new hires alike. At HRT we’re friends and colleagues – whether we are sharing a meal, playing the latest board game, or writing elegant code. We embrace a culture of togetherness that extends far beyond the walls of our office.

Feel like you belong at HRT? Our goal is to find the best people and bring them together to do great work in a place where everyone is valued. title: System Integration Engineer (System Engineer - Effector Development)
description:
The Destinus engineering team is seeking a Systems Engineer to lead the system-level definition and technical development of our effector programmes. This role sits at the centre of the development effort – bridging operational requirements and technical execution across propulsion, structures, avionics, and seeker.

The ideal candidate brings a defence systems background and understands the full development lifecycle of a guided effector – from ConOps and requirements through subsystem design, integration, and qualification. They are technically credible across multiple domains, rigorous in their systems thinking, and effective at driving alignment across disciplinary teams.

What You’ll Do

· Define and own system-level requirements for effector programmes – capturing operational needs, translating them into technical requirements, and maintaining traceability from ConOps through to subsystem specifications

· Develop and maintain ConOps and operational scenario definitions; work with the customer and programme stakeholders to ensure operational intent is correctly reflected in the system design

· Define and manage technical interfaces between subsystems (propulsion, warhead/pyrotechnics, structures, avionics, guidance, and GSE); own the ICD and IRS documentation

· Lead trade studies and make-or-buy analyses to identify the best technical and commercial solutions at system and subsystem level

· Identify and track critical components and subsystems; define mitigation strategies for technical risk and drive resolution through the engineering team

· Lead or support system design reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR) and prepare the associated technical baseline documentation

· Coordinate system integration activities across propulsion, structures, avionics, and external teams; ensure interfaces are closed and integration milestones are met

· Support verification and validation planning; define the V&V approach at system level and ensure it flows down to subsystem test plans

Requirements

What You’ll Need

· Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace, Systems, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field

· 5–8 years of systems engineering experience on defence or weapons system programmes – rockets, missiles, or guided weapons are a strong advantage; a background in aerospace or space launcher development is also suitable

· Proven experience defining and managing system requirements and interfaces across multi-disciplinary teams in a defence acquisition or development environment

· Hands-on experience with ConOps development, trade studies, and make-or-buy decision frameworks

· Familiarity with system design review processes (SRR, PDR, CDR) and the associated technical documentation

· Experience with V&V planning and requirements traceability; exposure to relevant standards (e.g. ARP4754, DEF STAN, MIL-STD, or equivalent) is an advantage

· Solid understanding of at least one key effector subsystem domain – propulsion, structures, avionics, or guidance – with the breadth to work credibly across all of them

· Structured, rigorous, and delivery-focused – able to drive technical decisions without getting lost in analysis

· Fluent in English; German is an advantage

title: Investment Analyst
description:
Updated: October 1, 2026

Title: Investment Analyst

Staff Group: Finance

Reports To: Senior Investment Analyst

Location: Boston, Massachusetts (hybrid onsite / remote)

Job Category: Program Specialist II

Hours/Week: 35

Purpose

We are seeking a motivated early-career investment professional to join our team as an Investment Analyst. This role provides responsibility for analyzing and reporting on values and impact investments, supporting proxy voting and company engagement, conducting climate analysis and measurement, and engaging with community and climate justice investments in the context of a sophisticated endowment fund. The Analyst will contribute to stewardship activities and support the ongoing development of the Common Endowment Fund’s investment and stewardship work.

Principal Responsibilities

  • Values Analysis and Reporting:
  • Produce reports and analyses on the Common Endowment Fund's (CEF) carbon footprint, Climate Justice and Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) exposures.
  • Support ongoing climate analysis, including emissions measurement, transition assessment, and climate-related risk and opportunity evaluation across the portfolio.
  • Proxy Voting and Stewardship:
  • Support execution and documentation of proxy voting activities in alignment with UUA policies and stewardship priorities.
  • Assist in developing proxy voting guidelines and analysis of company engagements and shareholder proposals.
  • Maintain records and provide analysis/research for the CEF's company advocacy and engagement activities.
  • Community Investment Research:
  • Maintain the investment pipeline, and conduct analysis and support development of Investment Memos, including financial characteristics, investment structure, and impact alignment.
  • Assist in tracking existing investments, monitoring impact metrics, and preparing portfolio and pipeline updates.
  • Manager Commentary Review:
  • Ensure receipt and review of all ongoing CEF manager commentaries and reports.
  • Performs other duties in the Investment Office as requested by supervisor, Vice President or President.

Qualifications

This position has a midpoint of $65,700. Compensation may vary based on factors such as experience, qualifications, and geographical location, with offers potentially ranging from 10-15% higher or lower than the midpoint. Requirements include:

  • 3-5 years of relevant experience
  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Sustainability, or a related field, or a bachelor’s degree in another field combined with relevant investment, financial, analytical, or related experience.
  • Excellent written and verbal financial or investment communication abilities.
  • Demonstrated interest in sustainable, impact and / or community investing, and / or stewardship and company engagement.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team.
  • Attention to detail and strong organizational skills.
  • Understanding of issues around anti-racism, anti-oppression, and multiculturalism
  • Work or lived experience with BIPOC communities is of particular value
  • Eagerness to work in an organization in which the dismantling of white supremacy is a high priority

How to Apply

People with disabilities, people of color, indigenous people, Hispanic/Latinx, and LGBTQ candidates are encouraged to apply. The UUA is committed to developing a diverse and talented staff team. If you are excited about this role, but are unsure whether you meet 100% of the requirements, we encourage you to inquire and/or apply. Please submit your resume and cover letter via our applicant portal (ADP WorkforceNow) on uua.org/jobs. If you have any questions, please reach out to careers@uua.org.

About the UUA

The Unitarian Universalist Association is a progressive religious denomination headquartered in Boston’s waterfront Fort Point Innovation District. Our faith community of more than 1,000 self-governing congregations brings to the world a vision of religious freedom, tolerance, and social justice. Our normal workweek is 35 hours, we pay 80% contribution towards health insurance premiums, 10% towards retirement (after one year), and have generous paid time-off policies. We are a great place to work, and we value diversity. The UUA is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to the full inclusion of all. As part of this commitment, the UUA will ensure that applicants and staff with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact the Department of Human Resources at careers@uua.org. For more information on the UUA, visit us online at UUA.org and uuworld.org.

Support for the Mission and Values of the Association

The Unitarian Universalist Association is a progressive and historic religious denomination. All UUA staff members are expected to perform their job duties in accordance with the UUA’s values, principles, and mission. Unitarian Universalism puts love at the center of our commitments, which embrace the Shared Values of justice, equity, transformation, interdependence, pluralism and generosity. The following points drawn from these Shared Values are of particular importance for the UUA’s work environment and staff culture:

  • Pluralism and generosity: We affirm the need for a human-centered workplace that allows our diverse staff to flourish. We also understand that our wider culture and society oppresses and denies human dignity, and we seek to counter the effects of that oppression in our hiring and workplace culture so that each person feels whole and valued.
  • Justice and equity: We speak openly and publicly of our support for social and political issues, including LGBTQ equity, racial justice, climate justice, gender equity, and reproductive justice.
  • Interdependence and transformation: We recognize that the liberation of all people is interwoven, and we work to counter patriarchy, white supremacy, colonialism, homophobia, transphobia, environmental exploitation, and other interrelated systems of marginalization.

Overview
