title: Sr. Benefits Associate (Level III)
description:
At Greenbrier, we do the hard work that matters. The Greenbrier Companies (NYSE:GBX) is powering the movement of products around the world as a leading designer, manufacturer and supplier of freight rail transportation equipment and services.

Greenbrier’s heritage of hard work and industrial innovation is celebrated at every level of our organization. We structure our business to support teams that deliver innovative solutions for our customers while positively impacting the world around us.

Greenbrier’s success begins with people. We believe in supporting our global workforce through our unwavering attention to Safety, Quality, Respect for People and Customer Satisfaction. Our Inclusion, Diversity, Engagement, Access and Leadership (IDEAL) commitment is rooted in these values, which lead to a culture where employees are engaged and feel good about coming to work every day.

Summary

The Benefit Associate III performs advanced administrative work supporting the day-to-day operation of the company’s employee benefits and leave programs. Working with limited supervision and within established policies and procedures, this position independently processes complex transactions, reviews data for accuracy, resolves routine and moderately complex issues, and escalates matters requiring policy interpretation or higher-level approval. The role serves as an experienced resource for employees and partners closely with Human Resources, Payroll, benefit carriers, leave administrators, and other vendors to provide accurate, timely, and employee-focused service.

The position requires strong organization, analytical ability, attention to detail, and sound judgment in applying established procedures. The employee manages multiple priorities and deadlines, identifies discrepancies, recommends practical process improvements, and uses advanced Microsoft Excel skills to support audits, reconciliations, tracking, and reporting.

Duties and Responsibilities

To perform this job successfully an individual must be able to perform the following essential duties satisfactorily. Other duties may be assigned to address business needs and changing business practices.

Benefits Administration

  • Administer employee benefit programs including medical, dental, vision, HSAs, FSAs, life insurance, disability, retirement, and voluntary benefits.
  • Support company wellness initiatives and related reporting.
  • Independently process new hire enrollments, qualifying life events, terminations, and annual open enrollment transactions in accordance with established procedures.
  • Maintain accurate employee benefit records within HRIS and benefits administration systems.
  • Audit benefit eligibility, deductions, invoices, and enrollment data to ensure accuracy.
  • Reconcile monthly carrier invoices and resolve discrepancies in a timely manner.
  • Partner with Payroll to ensure accurate benefit deductions and employer contributions.
  • Research and resolve routine and moderately complex employee questions regarding eligibility, coverage, claims, and benefit options; escalate exceptions and matters requiring policy interpretation.
  • Coordinate with insurance carriers, brokers, and third-party administrators to resolve issues.
  • Prepare reports, analyze benefit data, and identify trends using Microsoft Excel
  • Develop and maintain spreadsheets for benefits tracking, audits, reconciliations, and reporting.
  • Coordinate assigned annual benefits open enrollment activities, including employee communications, system testing, data validation, and system updates.

Leave Administration

  • Administer employee leave programs, including Family and Medical Leave (FMLA), paid family and medical leave, workers' compensation coordination, military leave, and other company leave policies.
  • Review leave requests for eligibility and coordinate required documentation.
  • Communicate with employees, managers, healthcare providers, and third-party leave administrators throughout the leave process.
  • Monitor leave timelines, certification deadlines, return-to-work dates, and intermittent leave usage.
  • Coordinate return-to-work processes
  • Maintain accurate leave records and ensure compliance with federal, state, and company leave requirements.
  • Partner with Payroll to ensure accurate pay status and benefit deductions during employee leaves.
  • Educate employees and managers on leave policies, procedures, and available resources.

Compliance & General Administration

  • Perform assigned administrative compliance activities related to COBRA, ACA, HIPAA, ERISA, FMLA, and other applicable federal, state, and local requirements using established procedures and timelines; identify discrepancies and escalate potential compliance concerns.
  • Maintain confidential employee information with the highest level of discretion.
  • Recommend and implement process improvements to increase efficiency and accuracy.
  • Complete assigned HR projects, audits, data reviews, and recurring or ad hoc reports, coordinating follow-up items through completion.

Qualifications

The following generally describes requirements to successfully perform the assigned duties.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field preferred, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in benefits and leave administration or Human Resources.
  • Demonstrated experience administering employee leave programs, including FMLA, and workers' compensation coordination.
  • Strong knowledge of employee benefits administration and applicable federal and state employment laws.
  • Excellent Microsoft Excel skills are required, including:
    • Pivot Tables
    • VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP
    • Advanced formulas and functions
    • Data validation
    • Conditional formatting
    • Sorting, filtering, and management of large data sets
    • Reporting and data analysis
  • Experience with HRIS, payroll, and leave management systems.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.
  • Excellent customer service, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining confidentiality.

Preferred Qualifications

  • PHR or SPHR certification.
  • Experience with third-party leave administrators and benefits administration platforms.
  • Knowledge of multi-state leave laws and paid family leave programs.
  • Experience supporting annual open enrollment and compliance audits.

title: Client Service Monitor
description:
Hope Mission Statement

The mission of Hope the Mission is to prevent, reduce and eliminate poverty, hunger, and homelessness by offering immediate assistance and long-term solutions.

Position Purpose and Summary

The Client Services Monitor (CSM) works directly on-site and is responsible for keeping participants safe, supporting daily operations, community standards and helping Hope the Mission's Interim Housing programs run smoothly. The CSM plays an important role in creating an environment that is safe, structured, and respectful — one where every participant is treated with dignity and fairness.

This position requires someone who shows up consistently, uses good judgment, and genuinely cares about serving people experiencing homelessness. Many participants in our programs have been through long periods of instability, crisis, and trauma. When a CSM shows up with calm, care, and compassion, it creates a sense of safety and routine that participants can count on as they work toward stable housing.

The CSM reports to the Program Manager or Assistant Program Manager and works alongside site staff to make sure the program runs well, meets contract requirements, and reflects Hope the Mission's values in every interaction.


Primary Duties and Responsibilities

Facility Maintenance and Sanitation

  • Assists with and facilitates routine cleaning of all facility areas to maintain cleanliness, safety, and operational readiness

  • Cleans and disinfects restrooms and shower areas after each use, without exception. Maintains sanitary and safe restroom and sink conditions at all times. Completes deep cleaning of restrooms and common areas.

  • Monitors and maintains hygiene areas and community areas; ensures resources are fully stocked, replenishing as needed.

  • Washes, dries, and prepares towels used for restroom and shower services

  • Monitors laundry rooms, restrooms, and common areas to ensure cleanliness and appropriate use

  • Maintains accurate shower and restroom usage logs

Participant Safety and Monitoring

  • Conducts required wellness checks each shift to ensure participant safety and well-being

  • Monitors participant movement, common areas, and site activity to promote safety and program compliance

  • Conducts routine site walk-throughs and safety checks during assigned shifts

  • Supports contraband control and safety procedures in accordance with agency policy

  • Responds to incidents and emergencies using trauma-informed de-escalation techniques and follows all incident reporting protocols

  • Supports emergency responses — including medical emergencies, overdoses, and evacuations — until leadership or first responders arrive

Participant Services and Engagement

  • Provides direct, respectful assistance to participants, including answering questions, responding to requests, and connecting participants to appropriate staff or resources

  • Assists with participant intake, orientation, and explanation of site guidelines as directed by management

  • Distributes hygiene supplies including soap, shampoo, towels, and related items to participants as needed

  • Supports meal service, supply distribution, and general operational duties as assigned

Documentation and Reporting

  • Completes Daily Activity Reports (DARs) accurately, objectively, and in a timely manner

  • Conducts intake, exit, and case notes in HMIS where applicable

  • Assists with documentation related to participant movements, wellness concerns, or incidents as required

title: Director-Enterprise Data-Governance
description:
The Director, Enterprise Data & Governance is accountable for how MedRisk organization builds and manages its data capabilities, and how it governs both data and AI. This role will partner with leadership across the organization to establish and mature the enterprise data strategy, own the delivery and scaling of a modern data platform, and build and operate the governance function for data and AI systems.


This role will partner with leadership across Enterprise Architecture, Development, Infrastructure, and Security, with Analytics and Data Science leadership, and with business stakeholders in order to identify the source systems, data domains, and priority use cases the enterprise depends on, and to build a data platform that serves analytics, AI, and operational applications from a single governed foundation. Success requires translating business priorities into a sequenced roadmap that spans the platform itself, the data products built on it, and the decisions about which data the enterprise should acquire, retain, or source externally to support them.


In parallel, the role will build and lead MedRisk's data and AI governance function from the ground up, establishing the policies, standards, and oversight structures that govern data use and the development, deployment, and monitoring of AI systems. It shares accountability for consistency across the platform and the applications where data originate, setting the classification, ownership, stewardship, and quality expectations that are applied across the full path data travels. For AI governance, the role will partner closely with AI delivery teams and offices of the CISO, legal, and compliance to design an operating model that is embedded in how AI products are built and shipped, with review, approval, and monitoring integrated into the delivery lifecycle.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Enterprise Data Platform Delivery

  • Own delivery of the enterprise data lakehouse, including scope, sequencing, delivery commitments, and the transition from build into sustained operation.
  • Define the operating standards the platform is held to — reliability, availability, performance, data quality, and observability — and report against them to leadership.
  • Own the cost profile of the platform, establishing the consumption visibility, forecasting, and optimization practices that keep spend predictable as it scales.
  • Ensure the platform is built and operated in accordance with enterprise engineering standards for environment management, release discipline, and production support.
  • Lead the engineering and technical leaders responsible for the platform, setting expectations, developing the team, and building the bench needed to sustain it.
  • Manage the delivery partners supporting the platform build, ensuring external capacity accelerates delivery without eroding engineering standards or institutional knowledge.

Data Strategy & Data Products

  • Own and continuously evolve MedRisk's enterprise data strategy and multi-year roadmap, aligning platform, data product, and governance investments with business priorities
  • Define the strategy that transforms data into a reusable enterprise asset across domains and use cases.
  • Establish a portfolio of enterprise data products with named owners, documented consumption contracts, service expectations, and quality standards.
  • Own the strategy for acquiring and integrating external data, including evaluation of third-party and industry data sources, the business case for acquisition, and the licensing and permitted-use terms.
  • Deliver curated, AI/ML-ready data assets that allow the data science and AI engineering teams to move directly to model development.

Data Governance

  • Define and maintain enterprise standards for data classification, usage, stewardship, and lifecycle management.
  • Establish master and reference data, metadata, catalog, lineage, and semantic governance capabilities.
  • Own the governance strategy for complex data-use scenarios arising from corporate integrations, including navigating client-level data use restrictions across legacy contracts and developing defensible approaches to data commingling that balance client trust with the organization's ability to build enterprise-wide intelligence from its data assets.
  • Ensure privacy and regulatory requirements are embedded in platform architecture and data product design, in partnership with the CISO, Legal, and Compliance.
  • Serve as the primary internal owner for data governance audit and client due-diligence requests.

AI Governance

  • Build and lead MedRisk's AI governance function, establishing the policies, standards, and oversight structures that govern how AI systems are developed, deployed, and monitored across the enterprise.
  • Establish a repeatable governance operating model for intake, review, approval, and monitoring of AI systems.
  • Run AI products through formal governance review prior to and during production use, assessing risk, documentation, monitoring, and control adequacy.
  • Maintain an inventory of AI systems in production and in development, with governance status tracked for each.
  • Track and interpret the evolving regulatory landscape for AI and data use — including NIST AI RMF, emerging state and federal AI regulation, and applicable healthcare and insurance data requirements — and translate external requirements into internal policy.
  • Serve as the escalation point for AI risk questions raised by clients, auditors, or internal stakeholders, and report governance status, risk posture, and program maturity to executive leadership.
  • Develop documentation and facilitate training necessary for governance standards to be understood and followed by technical and business teams.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • 12+ years in enterprise data, data platform, or analytics leadership, including 5+ years at the Director or Vice President level with delivery accountability.
  • Proven accountability for delivering and operating a modern cloud data platform or lakehouse at enterprise scale.
  • Demonstrated ownership of an enterprise data strategy end to end — defined it, sequenced it, and delivered against it over multiple years.
  • Track record establishing reusable enterprise data products with defined ownership and consumption contracts.
  • Demonstrated experience building a data or AI governance function from the ground up.
  • Strong working knowledge of AI governance frameworks and standards (e.g., NIST AI RMF) and the general shape of emerging AI regulation, with the ability to translate frameworks into enforced operational policy.
  • Experience operating in highly regulated data environments handling PHI or other sensitive data, with working familiarity of frameworks such as HIPAA/HITECH, SOC 2, or HITRUST.
  • Comfort operating as a policy-setting authority with executive-level accountability, including presenting to and being questioned by senior leadership, clients, and auditors.
  • Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred

  • Experience in workers' compensation, healthcare services, or property and casualty insurance.
  • Experience with governance challenges arising from M&A or business integration — contract-driven data use restrictions, data commingling decisions, and multi-entity data strategy.
  • Experience acquiring, licensing, and integrating third-party or industry data at enterprise scale.
  • Familiarity with Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, and Power BI.

title: Media Systems Architecture Intern
description:
Do you want to learn how Video and Display hardware is designed and integrated into modern computing systems? Arm has an internship opportunity in our Media architecture team, combining computer architecture, hardware design and software development!

Arm’s Sophia Antipolis design centre is located at the heart of one of Europe’s largest technology parks, between the mountains and the Mediterranean Sea. The site has contributed to many Arm technologies used in consumer and computing products worldwide.

Job Overview:

Modern Systems-on-Chip (SoCs) integrate sophisticated Video and Display hardware with many components, interfaces, clock domains and power domains. Describing these systems accurately and keeping architectural information consistent throughout the design process presents an interesting engineering challenge!

The goal of this internship is to explore tools and technologies for modelling and automating the design of Arm Media subsystems.

The project will investigate machine-readable descriptions of hardware architectures. These models can capture components, interfaces, connectivity, clock and power domains, allowing architectural information to be checked and reused across different stages of hardware development.

What you could be doing as a Media Systems Architecture Intern:

  • Work alongside experienced architects, the internship will provide exposure to the architecture and integration of Media hardware within an SoC.
  • Develop machine-readable models of hardware subsystems using Python and system modelling tools.
  • Explore how these models can automate engineering tasks, check architectural consistency and improve the flow of information between architecture and hardware implementation teams.
  • Hands-on prototyping and evaluation using representative Media subsystem designs.

We are looking for individuals who:

  • Are currently enrolled and studying towards a Master Degree in Computer Science or Electronic Engineering. Candidates with alternative degrees will also be considered if they have relevant experience.
  • Possess programming experience, preferably using Python,
  • Have a good understanding of computer architecture or digital hardware fundamentals.
  • Demonstrate an interest in system architecture, hardware modelling and design automation.

Qualities that will help your application stand out:

  • Knowledge of System-on-Chip architecture, hardware interfaces or hardware description languages such as SystemVerilog or Verilog would be beneficial.
  • Experience with Python development, clock and power management, or graphics, video and display systems.

Additional Information:

We encourage early applications as we review them on a first come/first served basis.

Arm Internships require you to be enrolled in a higher education degree.

The internship duration is 6 months, starting in 2027.

French Law requires students to complete an internship agreement (Convention de Stage). This is a tripartite agreement signed by the student, their home university and host organization, that facilitates an internship in France. It is the contract defining all the essential points of the internship: duration, missions, remuneration and benefits, insurance in the event of an accident, etc.

It is preferable that Arm's own template of the agreement is used. Successful applicants will be required to provide contact details of the appropriate university representatives in order to have the agreement signed.

Please note we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants must have the right to work in the country where the internship is based, without relying on sponsorship by Arm, for the full duration of the internship

In Return:

Working on interesting new projects with leaders in the field is exciting, but we also know how important it is to receive support. That's why throughout your internship, you can expect regular feedback and development opportunities, social activities to connect with your peers, an end of internship celebration, plus the opportunity to be *considered for future Graduate positions (*subject to performance). #getreadytogrow

In addition to a competitive salary of €27,000 per annum, our on-the-job learning and mentoring/buddy schemes provide unparalleled learning and networking opportunities from the best in the industry.

While previous Mercedes-Benz or Sprinter experience is highly desirable, it is not required. We are particularly interested in technicians with proven diesel diagnostic and repair experience from commercial truck, fleet, European automotive, or other professional service environments.

The right candidate will be comfortable diagnosing complex mechanical, electrical, emissions, and drivability concerns and performing repairs ranging from routine maintenance to major engine, drivetrain, and chassis work.

  • Maintain required Mercedes-Benz training and certifications following employment.
  • Assist in the development of less-experienced technicians and apprentices when appropriate.

Qualifications

  • Professional diesel repair and diagnostic experience strongly preferred.
  • Experience diagnosing diesel engine performance, fuel, emissions, electrical, or drivability concerns.
  • Experience with Sprinter, Mercedes-Benz, European vehicles, medium-duty trucks, commercial vehicles, or fleet maintenance is highly desirable.
  • Ability to perform mechanical repairs beyond routine maintenance, including engine, drivetrain, suspension, brake, and emissions-system repairs.

  • Ability to work some Saturdays.
  • Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record.

What We're Looking For

We are looking for more than someone who can replace parts. The ideal Sprinter Technician is a capable diagnostic technician who understands diesel systems and knows how to systematically determine the cause of a failure.

Candidates with experience in any of the following environments are encouraged to apply:

  • Mercedes-Benz or Sprinter dealerships

  • Ford Transit, Ram ProMaster, or similar commercial-vehicle platforms

Mercedes-Benz experience is an advantage, but we are willing to provide manufacturer-specific training to an experienced diesel technician who brings the right diagnostic foundation, work ethic, and commitment to quality.

Product Delivery and Backlog Ownership, 30%

Essential Responsibilities:

• IT Strategy and Governance: Develop and maintain a multi-year information technology and digital strategy aligned with organizational priorities and measurable outcomes.

Translate complex technical issues into clear operational and financial implications.

Maintain policies, controls, security awareness, incident response, vulnerability management, identity and access management, and third-party risk oversight.

Coordinate technology response plans with organizational emergency preparedness and continuity activities.

• Digital Transformation and Innovation: Identify, evaluate, and responsibly implement technologies that improve workflows, service reliability, employee experience, and organizational effectiveness. Establish governance for automation, artificial intelligence, and other emerging technologies, including privacy, security, ethical use, and change-management considerations.

150 Hanscom Drive, Bedford, MA 01730-2630 | 781-863-2213 | www.BostonMedFlight.org

title: Product Engineering Lead, Keet (100% Remote, Worldwide)
description:
Join Tether and Shape the Future of Digital Finance

At Tether, we’re not just building products, we’re pioneering a global financial revolution. Our cutting-edge solutions empower businesses—from exchanges and wallets to payment processors and ATMs—to seamlessly integrate reserve-backed tokens across blockchains. By harnessing the power of blockchain technology, Tether enables you to store, send, and receive digital tokens instantly, securely, and globally, all at a fraction of the cost. Transparency is the bedrock of everything we do, ensuring trust in every transaction.

Innovate with Tether

Tether Finance: Our innovative product suite features the world’s most trusted stablecoin, USDT, relied upon by hundreds of millions worldwide, alongside pioneering digital asset tokenization services.

But that’s just the beginning:

Tether Power: Driving sustainable growth, our energy solutions optimize excess power for Bitcoin mining using eco-friendly practices in state-of-the-art, geo-diverse facilities.

Tether Data: Fueling breakthroughs in AI and peer-to-peer technology, we reduce infrastructure costs and enhance global communications with cutting-edge solutions like KEET, our flagship app that redefines secure and private data sharing.

Tether Education: Democratizing access to top-tier digital learning, we empower individuals to thrive in the digital and gig economies, driving global growth and opportunity.

Tether Evolution: At the intersection of technology and human potential, we are pushing the boundaries of what is possible, crafting a future where innovation and human capabilities merge in powerful, unprecedented ways.

Why Join Us?

Keet is a fully peer-to-peer messaging and video calling app built on Holepunch's P2P stack. There are no servers, no middlemen, and no data harvesting. People talk directly to each other, with end-to-end encryption by design.

We're taking Keet to a billion users, competing head-on with WhatsApp and Telegram. Product sets the direction. We're looking for a Product Engineering Lead to turn that direction into features people love, built to a standard that holds up at global scale.

You lead the teams that build Keet's features: the API team, which adds feature-focused APIs to Keet's core, and the frontend team, which builds the React app on top, each with its own lead. You report directly to the CTO and take direction from product. Product owns the what and the why. You own the how and the engineering bar. The split is roughly 70% engineering leadership and 30% product.

You're a combination of three things. You're an engineering leader who has helped teams ship consumer products at speed. You have real product sense and can partner with PMs as an equal, shaping what gets built, not just executing it. And you have an intuition for distributed, local-first systems, so you can work fluently on top of a P2P engine without needing to build it yourself.

Responsabilities

Engineering

  • Run the API and frontend teams day to day: unblocking, reviewing, and keeping them shipping.

  • Set and hold a high engineering bar for performance, reliability, and clean APIs.

  • Own the technical design of features and the API surface between Keet's core and the app.

  • Make sure the API team works closely with our deep tech teams on code reviews, design, and anything that touches the engine.

Product Partnership

  • Work alongside Keet's product managers to turn vision and roadmap into scoped, buildable work.

  • Push back when scope and reality don't match, and propose better paths when they exist.

  • Bring an engineering perspective to product decisions, especially where P2P opens doors that centralized apps can't.

  • Help the team move fast, using AI tools and quick prototypes to validate ideas before committing to them.

Leadership

  • Create clarity around team goals and make sure everyone knows what success looks like.

  • Mentor team leads to build strong team operating systems, improve how their teams work with others, and grow as leaders.

  • Lead by example: roll up your sleeves when the team needs it, and step back when they're ready to own it.

Requirements

  • Experience managing engineers or engineering leads who ship consumer product, ideally in chat, calling, or social apps.

  • Strong product sense: you can tell a good feature from a busy one.

  • Intuition for distributed and local-first systems. Offline-first and eventual consistency should feel natural. You don't need P2P protocol expertise, because our core abstracts it away.

  • Deep JavaScript and React.

  • Initiative, curiosity, resilience, and the ability to give and receive direct critique.

  • Bonus: experience with local-first apps, CRDTs or sync engines, offline-capable mobile or desktop apps, or open source.

Every day we partner with customers to create healthier, tastier and more sustainable products that are consumed by billions of people across the world. Our vision is to be our customers' most valued partner, creating a world of sustainable nutrition. A career with Kerry offers you an opportunity to shape the future of food while providing you opportunities to explore and grow in a truly global environment.

Where You'll Work

If you are a dependable, safety-minded maintenance professional who enjoys solving problems and supporting a manufacturing team, we encourage you to apply for the Maintenance Technician Level 1 position at our Evansville facility.

Our Evansville, IN, location is part of our Coatings division, and creates various breading, batter, and coating blends for Kerry brands and customers. We feel good about our products that make our food taste better. Our employees care about their community, their team and the results we create every day. If you’re looking for a manufacturing facility where you can build a career and have fun while you do it, we might be the team for you! We are part of the Evansville Local Labor Union 561, and we are located at 1515 Park Street, Evansville, IN.

Compensation Data

The pay rate for this position is $33.00 per hour. Kerry offers a competitive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, paid time off, a 401(k) plan with employee and company contribution opportunities, Employee Share Plan, Life, disability, and accident insurance. This job posting is anticipated to expire on 1/3/2027.

We may use artificial intelligence tools to support the review and assessment of applications and assist with scheduling interviews. We do not use AI to make decisions during the interview process. All candidate assessments and employment decisions are made by human recruitment and leadership teams.

What You'll Do

3rd Shift is 10 pm to 6:30 am

Maintenance Bonus $2500 sign on bonus $250 after two weeks no attendance issues. $2250 after 120 days.

Join Our Team!

We are seeking a Maintenance Technician Level 1 to help keep our Evansville facility operating safely, reliably, and efficiently. Reporting to the Maintenance Supervisor, you will troubleshoot, repair, install, and maintain production equipment, facility systems, and property. This role is a strong fit for a hands-on maintenance professional who stays focused, responds positively to changing priorities, and enjoys learning and sharing new skills.

What You’ll Do

  • Perform scheduled preventive maintenance, inspections, adjustments, troubleshooting, and repairs on production and facility equipment.
  • Maintain and repair equipment such as mixers, conveyors, compressors, pumps, bearings, sprockets, chains, sensors, and related components.
  • Use hand tools, power tools, welders, drill presses, grinders, cutting equipment, and other metalworking equipment safely.
  • Install new equipment and complete building and grounds maintenance as assigned.
  • Document work performed, labor hours, repairs, and installations in SAP work orders and notifications.
  • Learn production processes and equipment to provide effective support to production team members.
  • Identify abnormal or critical conditions, communicate safety or downtime risks, and seek guidance when an issue is outside your knowledge or authority.
  • Recommend equipment or procedures for preventive maintenance programs and help develop long-term solutions to recurring maintenance issues.
  • Work with contractors, vendors, supervisors, site leaders, and production personnel to support timely, accurate repairs.
  • Participate in predictive maintenance, continuous improvement, and food safety activities.
  • Maintain strong housekeeping and sanitation standards and follow all safety, quality, Good Manufacturing Practices, EPA, Hazmat, and OSHA requirements.
  • Operate forklifts and aerial lifts and provide support in the parts storeroom as needed.
  • Complete special projects and provide break relief to other maintenance employees as assigned.

What You'll Need To Succeed

  • At least 1 year of relevant maintenance experience.
  • A two-year degree in industrial technology or advanced manufacturing is preferred.
  • Previous experience in a food manufacturing facility is preferred.
  • Mechanical repair, general welding, and minor electrical troubleshooting skills.
  • Ability to independently complete preventive maintenance and work-order repairs.
  • Ability to replace like-for-like electronic components, including sensors and bin indicators.
  • Ability to work independently and collaborate closely with production and maintenance team members to solve complex problems.
  • Ability to prioritize work and ask for guidance when needed.
  • Working knowledge of SAP or the ability to learn a computerized maintenance management system.
  • Reliable attendance and the ability to complete work accurately and on time.

Work Environment and Physical Requirements

This position works in an industrial manufacturing environment that may include high noise levels, wet floors, steam equipment, confined spaces, and outdoor temperatures ranging from below 0°F to above 100°F. The role requires frequent climbing, crawling, bending, twisting, and work from ladders or aerial lifts, sometimes more than 20 feet above the floor. Employees must be able to regularly lift 25 pounds and occasionally lift 50 pounds, use force to operate tools and equipment, and meet the vision and hearing requirements needed to safely diagnose equipment issues.

title: Software Engineer
description:
Software Engineer

Salary: £47,200 - £59,000 DOE + Benefits + Bonus
Location: Birmingham

Closing Date: 20th October

We care deeply about inclusive working practices and diverse teams. If you'd prefer to work part-time or as a job-share, we'll facilitate this wherever we can; whether to help you meet other commitments or to help you strike a great work-life balance.

About

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to join our growing Engineering team at ParkIT, designing, building and operating software across our cloud platform.

ParkIT is part of BookFlowGo, Holiday Extras Group’s B2B parking technology offering. BookFlowGo brings together pre-booking technology, parking operations software and hardware innovation to help airports, cities and mobility hubs run smarter, more efficient parking operations. Together, Parkspace by Chauntry, ParkIT and Future Generation Services (FGS) create a connected parking ecosystem that helps operators maximise revenue, optimise capacity and make parking more seamless for travellers.

At ParkIT, we build software that helps parking operations teams work smarter. ParkIT was created after identifying a need to move complex airport parking operations away from manual, paper-based processes. Today, our technology helps operators make more efficient, data-driven decisions and keep vehicle movements flowing smoothly.

This is a hands-on role where you’ll work primarily with Node.js, React and TypeScript, collaborating with Product Managers and fellow engineers to turn real operational challenges into scalable services and intuitive user experiences.

AI is part of how we build software at ParkIT. You’ll be expected to use AI tools throughout development, from exploring a codebase and testing ideas to implementation, review and documentation. You’ll help us develop effective ways of working with these tools, while using your engineering judgement to question their output and take responsibility for the software you deliver.

You don’t need experience with a particular AI tool, agent harness or AI-first team to apply. We’re looking for a strong software engineer who is curious, willing to learn and ready to make AI a regular part of their work. We expect you to experiment, share what works and adapt as the tools develop.

The Role

By joining our team, you'll:

  • Design, implement, and maintain backend services, frontend applications, and APIs using Node.js, React, and TypeScript.
  • Take ownership of features from initial understanding and technical design through to deployment, monitoring and improvement.
  • Work with Product Managers, engineers, data specialists and DevOps colleagues to turn requirements into clear, working software.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools for codebase exploration, research, design, implementation, testing, debugging, refactoring, documentation and review.
  • Critically review and validate AI-assisted output for correctness, security, performance and maintainability before it becomes part of our products.
  • Write unit, integration, component and end-to-end tests that safeguard reliability and meaningful behaviour.
  • Build and integrate APIs, distributed services and cloud-native components on Google Cloud Platform.
  • Contribute to CI/CD pipelines and release processes that support safe, repeatable delivery.
  • Take ownership of debugging, root-cause analysis, optimisation and the resolution of production issues.
  • Participate in code reviews and architectural discussions, and help us continuously improve our engineering practices.

What you can bring to our team

  • Strong professional experience with Node.js, React and TypeScript in production environments.
  • A solid understanding of modern JavaScript and TypeScript, including asynchronous programming and sound type design.
  • Experience building and operating cloud-based web applications, backend services and distributed systems.
  • Experience with API design, databases and the integration of services across a wider platform.
  • Strong grounding in testing practices, including unit, integration and automated testing; experience with Jest and TDD is beneficial.
  • Experience with cloud platforms, preferably Google Cloud Platform, together with Git, Docker and CI/CD workflows.
  • A willingness to use AI coding assistants and agentic tools as part of everyday software delivery, and to learn how to use them effectively.
  • Strong technical judgement when working with AI: you can provide appropriate context and constraints, critically review generated output, and identify incorrect, insecure or unsuitable suggestions. You remain accountable for the work you deliver.
  • An analytical and curious approach, with the persistence to investigate complex systems and solve real-world problems.
  • Excellent communication skills and a collaborative, pragmatic approach to delivery.

How we hire for this role

We know your time is precious, so we keep our recruitment process as quick and easy as possible. If we believe you might be a match for a job you’ve applied for, you’ll enter our hiring process as follows:

  • Initial pre-screen
  • Tech task
  • F2F Interview at the office

Cultivating a diverse and inclusive culture is paramount for us.

Why choose ParkIT?

We combine innovative technologies with field-based outreach to find and engage these members. We then apply a model of care designed to re-connect them to primary care, address the Health-Related Social Needs (HRSNs) that contribute to their disengagement and present barriers to care, and provide them with the means and knowledge to take more control over their healthcare. The Chief People Officer (CPO) is the senior executive responsible for AKBH’s people, culture, workforce, organizational learning, communications, and community management strategy. The CPO serves as a strategic advisor to the CEO, executive leadership, and, as requested, the Board of Directors on organizational health, workforce strategy, leadership capability, succession, employment risk, culture, communications, and other significant people-related matters.

The CPO leads Human Resources, Training, Community Relations and Communications, ensuring these functions strengthen organizational effectiveness, workforce capability, employee experience, and AKBH’s ability to achieve its mission and strategic priorities.

  • Lead the HR, Training, and Community Relations and Communications departments, establishing strategic direction, priorities, accountability, performance expectations, and effective coordination across functions.
  • Advise the CEO, executive leadership, and, as requested, the Board on organizational health, workforce trends and risk, succession, executive compensation, culture, and other significant people-related matters.

title: Regional Environmental Protection Specialist
description:
Gryphon Environmental is hiring a Regional Environmental Protection Specialist to keep U.S. Army Reserve facilities across Connecticut, New York, and New Jersey in compliance with environmental law. You will be the environmental point of contact for the facilities in your region, on site most of the week, working directly with the people who run them.

This is a field job. About 70% of your time is spent visiting your assigned facilities. The rest is split between working from home and an office at a 99th Readiness Division facility, with Fort Totten as your base. Your job is to make sure each facility is operated and maintained in line with Federal, State, and local environmental laws and regulations, Executive Orders, and DoD, Army, and Army Reserve regulations and policy.

If you like being out of the office, solving real compliance problems, and owning a territory, this is a good fit. It is also a strong role for someone early in an environmental career who wants broad exposure across nearly every media area.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Internal Assessments

  • Perform internal environmental assessments of your assigned facilities in accordance with Federal, State, and local regulations, DoD regulations, the USACE Environmental Assessment and Management (TEAM) Guides, and applicable checklists.
  • Document site visits and findings in the appropriate Army databases.
  • Conduct follow-up visits at any facility with Class 1 or Class 2 findings.
  • Update the Installation Corrective Action Plan (ICAP) as needed.

External Assessments

  • Support the 99th RD during external environmental assessments.

Site Assistance Visits (SAVs)

  • Conduct environmental SAVs for every facility in your area of responsibility.

Program Support

  • Provide general environmental support to the 99th RD and serve as the technical point of contact for environmental agencies, organizations, contractors, and other executive agents of the 99th RD.
  • Deliver environmental compliance training to facility personnel.
  • Collect stormwater and wastewater samples to support compliance with applicable permits.
  • Provide technical assistance to the Environmental Division's programs and projects, including research, analysis, development, coordination, and management, under the direction of the 99th RD environmental staff and in coordination with the Operations Team.

MEDIA AREAS YOU'LL WORK IN

You should have working knowledge of the areas below, or the drive to learn them:

  • Hazardous and solid waste
  • Pollution prevention and waste minimization
  • Spill response
  • Stormwater, wastewater, and drinking water
  • Air quality
  • Underground and aboveground storage tanks
  • National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA)
  • Cultural and natural resources
  • Integrated pest management
  • Remediation
  • Toxic Substances Control Act (asbestos, lead-based paint, PCBs, and radon)
  • Other media areas as required

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • B.S. in Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related field, and at least 2 years of environmental compliance or field experience. An M.S. counts as 2 years of experience.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to work with people at every level of an organization.
  • Confidence and willingness to give presentations and lead training sessions for small and large groups.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Microsoft SharePoint, and the willingness and ability to learn software systems specific to the Army Reserve.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Valid U.S. driver's license.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Department of the Army background investigation.
  • Access to a reliable automobile. Use of a personal vehicle is mandatory for this position.
  • Willingness to travel. Travel is about 70% of the job, mostly within the assigned region, with some travel outside it.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

  • 2 to 3 years of environmental compliance experience.

title: 2D FX Artists (mid- senior)

At Stellar, we aim to build a studio where people actually want to work. We face productions inevitable ups and downs as a supportive, truly connected team, prioritizing open communication over anyone working in isolation. We value honesty, creativity, and looking out for one another.

We are staffing up for a new Marvel Studios streaming series, and we are looking for talented 2D FX Artists across all experience levels to create and animate stunning effects for the show!

Whether you are a Mid level artist expanding your technical toolkit, or a Senior designing complex supernatural sequences, we want your artistic eye on our team.

In this role, success looks like:

Artistic Execution and Animation

Pipeline and Workflow

  • Maintain and communicate a strong knowledge of innovative 2D FX animation technologies, sharing best practices with the rest of the team.

The Requirements

Must Haves:

  • Experience:

  • Enjoy learning how software interacts with hardware and approaching technical problems methodically.

Qualities that will help your application stand out:

  • Practical experience gained through university work, personal projects, competitions, internships, open-source contributions, or similar activities.
  • Experience debugging software or hardware using tools such as GDB, JTAG, oscilloscopes, or logic analysers.
  • An analytical and collaborative approach, with the ability to communicate ideas clearly and an interest in building dependable, safety-focused software.

Additional Information:

We encourage early applications as we review them on a first come/first served basis.

In Return:

You’ll receive a starting salary of €64,500, alongside a comprehensive rewards package. As you develop in role, you’ll have clear opportunities to progress within the salary range at Arm. With mid-year and year-end reviews, you’ll have two formal progression windows each year, recognising your growth.

You can also attend our “Grad-teach-Grads” workshops, guest speaker series, and social events to expand your knowledge. If you’d like to get more involved, you can join the Graduate Committee to further develop your planning, networking, and coordination skills.

You’ll be invited to our Global Graduate Conference (GGC) — an annual event where graduates hear from executive leaders, guest speakers, and build lasting connections.

With many of our leaders and technical specialists having originally joined as a Graduate, will you be next?

title: Senior IT Analyst
description:
Location: Office Location Decatur, AR (May consider office location at another plant)
Travel: 30–50% across the United States and Canada as needed (Mishawaka, IN - Drummondville, QC - Other locations when added)
Reports To: Group IT Manager

About United Petfood

United Petfood is a private label producer of high-quality dry & wet pet food, biscuits and snacks. We are a Belgian family business with 25 high-tech pet kitchens in Europe and the US.

Joining us means joining an international, passionate, and driven team with one common goal: a healthy planet filled with healthy pets! But it doesn’t stop there—we truly care about building encouraging, supportive, long-lasting partnerships, both inside as well as outside of our fast-growing family company. By only working with the very best ingredients and most innovative technology available, we ensure a place in which you can grow, bloom, and make thousands of pets happy worldwide!

Check out our website: United Petfood Producers USA, Inc.

Position Summary

The Senior IT Analyst for North America serves as the primary regional Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (D365 F&O) expert supporting United Petfood's U.S. and Canadian operations.

As the first dedicated ERP resource based in North America, this position will bridge the time and operational gap between our North American facilities and central ERP team in Europe. The Senior IT Analyst will support the full ERP lifecycle—from business process, analysis and implementation through configuration, training, go-live, and ongoing optimization.

This is a hands-on role requiring both strong D365 F&O expertise and the ability to partner effectively with plant operations, finance, supply chain, warehouse, IT, and external implementation teams. The successful candidate will balance local business requirements with United Petfood's global ERP standards while helping build scalable, sustainable processes across our growing North American operations.

Duties & Responsibilities

D365 F&O Implementation & Support

  • Serve as the primary D365 F&O subject matter expert for United Petfood's North American operations.
  • Support the full D365 F&O deployment lifecycle, including discovery, requirements gathering, process design, configuration, testing, data migration, go-live, stabilization, and post-implementation support.
  • Perform hands-on D365 F&O configuration and functional setup to support business and manufacturing requirements.
  • Troubleshoot functional and system issues and coordinate resolution with Group IT, business stakeholders, and external partners.
  • Support ongoing system enhancements, upgrades, process improvements, and optimization initiatives.
  • Help maintain a reliable, scalable, and sustainable D365 F&O environment as the North American business continues to grow.

Business Process & Solution Design

  • Partner with plant managers, finance, planning, warehouse, supply chain, and other key stakeholders to understand business processes, challenges, and system requirements.
  • Translate business requirements into clear functional and technical specifications.
  • Evaluate requirements against United Petfood's central ERP blueprint and recommend solutions that balance global standardization with legitimate local business needs.
  • Identify opportunities to improve processes through D365 F&O functionality, automation, and standardization.
  • Guide stakeholders through changing or incomplete requirements using a structured, solution-oriented approach.
  • Support process design across multiple sites while accounting for applicable U.S. and Canadian operational and regulatory requirements.

ERP Governance & Global Collaboration

  • Serve as the North American counterpart to United Petfood's central ERP team in Europe.
  • Maintain alignment with global ERP architecture, standards, processes, and governance requirements.
  • Communicate regional priorities, challenges, and requirements to Group IT and the central ERP team.
  • Participate in cross-regional ERP initiatives and collaborate with global stakeholders on system improvements and future-state design.
  • Accommodate occasional early meetings or adjusted schedules when necessary to collaborate effectively with European colleagues.

Implementation Partner & Integration Management

  • Work closely with United Petfood's systems integrator and other external technology partners supporting D365 F&O configuration, development, integrations, and larger project initiatives.
  • Define project requirements, scope work, and provide clear functional and technical direction to external partners.
  • Review and validate partner-delivered solutions to ensure they meet business requirements, technical expectations, and global ERP standards.
  • Coordinate ERP integration requirements involving systems such as MES, packaging equipment, weighbridge and scale systems, EDI, and other manufacturing technologies.
  • Identify and escalate project risks, system issues, and implementation concerns when appropriate.

Training, Adoption & Continuous Improvement

  • Develop and deliver practical D365 F&O training for end users, key users, and business stakeholders.
  • Provide hands-on support at plant locations during implementations, migrations, go-live activities, and stabilization periods.
  • Promote consistent system usage and adoption across North American facilities.
  • Develop and maintain appropriate process, configuration, training, and support documentation.
  • Gather user feedback and identify opportunities to improve functionality, processes, reporting, and the overall user experience.
  • Support knowledge transfer between North American users, Group IT, and external partners.

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum of 6 years of hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations in a functional, technical, or combined capacity.
  • Demonstrated D365 F&O experience across multiple environments, organizations, or implementations.
  • Experience supporting full-cycle ERP implementations, from initial requirements and design through go-live and post-implementation support.
  • Experience with multi-site and/or international ERP implementations.
  • Strong hands-on D365 F&O configuration and troubleshooting capabilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to gather, analyze, and translate business requirements into functional and technical solutions.
  • Experience managing or directing external consultants, systems integrators, and implementation partners.
  • Strong understanding of business processes and the relationship between ERP systems and operational requirements.
  • Ability to work independently and take ownership of regional ERP priorities while collaborating effectively with a global team.
  • Professional fluency in English.
  • Ability and willingness to travel 30–50% throughout the United States and Canada, including occasional multi-week assignments supporting implementations, migrations, or other critical project activities.
  • Valid passport and ability to travel between the United States and Canada for business.
  • Authorization to work in the United States or Canada without employer sponsorship.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting D365 F&O within a manufacturing environment; process manufacturing experience strongly preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of D365 F&O Advanced Warehouse Management.
  • Technical or development experience within the D365 F&O technology stack.
  • Experience with ERP integrations involving MES, packaging systems, weighbridge and scale systems, EDI, or similar manufacturing technologies.
  • Experience supporting business operations in both the United States and Canada, including relevant tax, payroll, and regulatory considerations.
  • Professional proficiency in French is strongly preferred due to support of our Drummondville, Quebec facility.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
  • High level of ownership and ability to operate autonomously as the primary North American ERP resource.
  • Ability to balance global standards with practical local business requirements.
  • Strong business acumen and ability to understand operational processes beyond the technical ERP environment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with audiences ranging from shop-floor and operational employees to senior leadership and technical teams.
  • Ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, practical business language.
  • Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills across different functions, locations, and cultures.
  • Ability to prioritize competing demands and remain effective when requirements or priorities change.
  • Sound judgment when evaluating proposed solutions, configurations, customizations, and partner-delivered work.
  • Comfortable working within a lean, collaborative, and fast-changing international organization.

Workplace Safety

  • Follow all company safety, security, and site requirements while working at United Petfood facilities.
  • Participate in required safety training and comply with applicable plant safety and food safety requirements.
  • Follow applicable procedures when working in or supporting technology within manufacturing and production environments.
  • Immediately report unsafe conditions, incidents, near misses, or other safety concerns.

Why Join Us?

At United Petfood, we believe in investing in our employees and providing opportunities for growth and development. As our Senior IT Analyst — North America, you will have a direct and visible impact on the digital foundation supporting our growing North American operations.

This role offers significant autonomy and the opportunity to become a key link between our North American business, European ERP organization, and implementation partners. You will help shape how D365 F&O supports our facilities as we continue to grow while gaining exposure to operations across multiple locations and countries.

We offer competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and a collaborative international environment where ownership, initiative, and practical problem-solving are valued.

Equal Opportunity Employer: United Petfood Producers USA Inc. is an equal opportunity workplace. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF JOB

This position provides a variety of high-level administrative services in the Assessment Office. The UPI Coordinator will interpret, research, and evaluate all land records related to legal instruments before they are recorded in the Recorder of Deeds Office.


QUALIFICATIONS

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE

  1. High school diploma or equivalent and one year of experience within tax assessment, property appraisal, real estate, or other related field services, or any equivalent combination of education and experience that provides equivalent knowledge, skills, and abilities.
  2. Must possess current license from the State Board of Appraisal as a Certified Pennsylvania Evaluator (CPE); OR possess equivalent IAAO certification or other state certification and have the ability to acquire and maintain a CPE certification immediately; OR have the ability to possess a CPE certification within three years from hire.
  3. Valid Pennsylvania driver’s license.


Clearances:

  • Must have acceptable results on all criminal background checks including Act 34 PA State Police Criminal History, Act 151 PA Child Abuse, Drivers Background Check, and FBI clearances.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Deeds/Transfers

  • Examine deeds, deeds of trust, liens, judgments, easements, and encumbrances to verify legal descriptions of property.
  • Forward instruments to the Planning/GIS department when parcels are combined, split, or re-surveyed.
  • Collect and record data related to real estate transfers and instruments in a consistent and timely manner. Enter designated information into CAMA (Computer-Assisted Mass Appraisal) software. Enter sales information on the County Property Record Cards.
  • Review instruments for the type of interest transferred, the rights conveyed, and other conditions that could affect the arm’s-length nature of the sale.

  • Review the Homestead/Farmstead status for each parcel related to a transfer document and assist with entry, processing, and reporting related to the existing database and new applications. Assist in the maintenance of the Occupation Tax roll.

title: Senior RMF Specialist/ISSO (Rock Island Arsenal, IL)
description:
Akira Technologies is seeking a Senior RMF Specialist / Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO) to support the U.S. Army Materiel Command (AMC) at Rock Island Arsenal, Illinois. This role will provide senior-level cybersecurity and Risk Management Framework (RMF) expertise to guide DoD information systems through the full RMF lifecycle and achieve and maintain an Authority to Operate (ATO).

The ideal candidate has extensive hands-on experience with DoD RMF processes, eMASS, vulnerability management, security assessments, and continuous monitoring. This individual will work closely with system owners, security teams, assessors, and Authorizing Officials to ensure systems meet applicable DoD cybersecurity requirements and maintain an effective security posture.

This is an onsite position at the Rock Island Arsenal, IL. Security clearance of TS/SCI is required to support the role.

Job Responsibilities

  • Lead the full DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) lifecycle, from system categorization and security control selection through implementation, assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring.
  • Guide system owners and technical teams in meeting DoD cybersecurity, RMF, and ATO requirements for complex IT systems.
  • Develop, maintain, and update required RMF documentation, including System Security Plans (SSPs), Security Assessment Reports (SARs), Plans of Action & Milestones (POA&Ms), and supporting artifacts.
  • Manage the system's security posture and RMF lifecycle within eMASS, ensuring records, controls, assessments, artifacts, and authorization data remain accurate and current.
  • Coordinate and support ATO packages, including preparation for security assessments, AO reviews, authorization decisions, and ongoing authorization activities.
  • Implement and manage continuous monitoring activities to evaluate security control effectiveness and maintain visibility into system risk.
  • Conduct, analyze, and track vulnerability assessments using ACAS/Nessus, SCAP, and other applicable security compliance and vulnerability scanning tools.
  • Identify, document, prioritize, and track security vulnerabilities and compliance findings through remediation and closure.
  • Support configuration management, security patching, and system changes, assessing their potential impact on the system's security posture and authorization status.
  • Serve as a senior cybersecurity advisor to System Owners, ISSMs/ISSO, Security Control Assessors, Authorizing Officials (AOs), and technical stakeholders.
  • Communicate system risks, vulnerabilities, compliance gaps, and ATO status while providing recommendations for effective risk mitigation.
  • Maintain awareness of applicable DoD cybersecurity policies, NIST SP 800-53, RMF requirements, COMSEC considerations, and DoD 8570/8140 requirements.

Job Qualifications

  • 5+ years of dedicated, hands-on DoD RMF/ATO experience supporting complex information technology systems.
  • Demonstrated experience executing the DoD Risk Management Framework throughout the full system lifecycle.
  • Extensive hands-on experience managing RMF activities and documentation in eMASS.
  • Experience with ACAS/Nessus, SCAP, and other vulnerability assessment and security compliance tools.
  • Working knowledge of COMSEC requirements and their application within DoD environments.
  • Current IAT Level II certification, at minimum, or equivalent qualification.
  • Industry-standard cybersecurity or technical certifications relevant to assigned duties, such as CompTIA Security+, CCNA, RHCSA, MCSA, or equivalent.
  • Certifications must meet applicable DoD 8570/8140 requirements for the assigned position.
  • Strong understanding of DoD cybersecurity policies, security controls, vulnerability management, and ATO processes.
  • Ability to develop and maintain comprehensive RMF documentation and communicate security risks effectively.
  • Active Top Secret/SCI security clearance and ability to maintain the required clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting U.S. Army programs, installations, or enterprise IT environments.
  • Experience working directly with Authorizing Officials, ISSMs/ISSO, Security Control Assessors (SCAs), and system owners.
  • Experience supporting ATO packages through assessment and authorization.
  • Familiarity with NIST SP 800-53, RMF, and applicable DoD cybersecurity policies and standards.
  • Experience with continuous monitoring and ongoing authorization activities in a DoD environment.

description:

At Shepherd’s House Ministries our mission is to create safe, healing environments where all individuals feel valued, respected, and empowered to pursue personal growth and stability. We strive to feed the hungry, shelter the homeless, and walk alongside those facing life-controlling challenges such as trauma, addiction, and homelessness. Through emergency shelter, case management, and supportive services, we seek not only to address immediate needs but to foster lasting, positive change. Our vision is to help individuals break cycles of hardship and achieve meaningful transformation, ensuring that everyone in Central Oregon has the opportunity to find hope, stability, and healing.

We are seeking a passionate and mission-driven Software Engineer to help expand the impact of Shepherd’s House Ministries across all sites and advance this life-changing work.

The Software Engineer is accountable for building, maintaining, and improving ShelterOps to provide reliable, effective technology that supports staff in serving guests and carrying out SHM’s mission. This role develops and delivers high-quality software, responds to operational needs, and protects the accuracy, security, and confidentiality of participant data.

Strategic Work Expectations:

Technical Environment:

  1. TypeScript throughout. React on the front end, Node/Express and PostgreSQL on the back end. Hosted on AWS.
  2. Automated tests and checks on every change, with continuous integration and automated deployment.
  3. AI coding tools are used daily under a human review-and-merge workflow.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  1. Build and maintain ShelterOps features from conversation with staff through deployment, including database changes, API handlers, user interface, and tests.
  2. Pair regularly with the Head of Technology on design, implementation, and review.

  6. Support data-quality and reporting work for state and federal requirements.
  7. Respond to production issues and participate in maintenance, upgrades, and documentation.
  8. Maintain accurate, confidential handling of participant data in accordance with organizational policy and applicable law.

Education & Experience:

  1. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, completion of a software development program, or equivalent combination of education and demonstrated experience.

Understanding of financial services domains or actuarial/data integrations. Soft Skills Ownership‑driven, autonomous, and accountable. Strong written and verbal communication; able to collaborate across technical and non‑technical teams. Passionate about craftsmanship, documentation, and continuous improvement. Experience 6+ years’ experience building and operating backend systems in production. Proven track record designing and maintaining high‑scale, mission‑critical services in cloud environments (AWS preferred). Experience delivering greenfield systems and evolving legacy platforms incrementally. Demonstrated impact in agile, product‑led, high‑stakes settings. Prior experience in regulated or financial services environments is advantageous. Qualifications Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline (or equivalent practical experience). Relevant certifications beneficial (e.g., AWS Certified Developer/Solutions Architect; domain‑specific security certifications). Nice‑to‑Have AWS Alignment Services: EC2, EKS, Lambda, API Gateway, ALB/NLB, RDS/Aurora, Dynamo DB, SQS/SNS, Kinesis, Elasti Cache/Redis, Secrets Manager, Cognito, Cloud Watch, X‑Ray. Practices: Infrastructure‑as‑Code collaboration with Dev Ops (Terraform/Cloud Formation), cost‑aware designs, and security‑first architectures aligned to CIS and IAM best practices. What Success Looks Like Measurable improvements in latency, throughput, and error rates against defined SLOs. Clearly defined and documented service boundaries with stable, versioned APIs. Robust test coverage and automated quality gates in CI/CD. Zero‑trust principles applied across services with least‑privilege access and strong auditability.
