About American Jewish University

American Jewish University (AJU)’s mission is singularly focused on the future of Jewish life by training and educating the next generation of rabbis, educators, professionals, and lay leaders, and creating innovative, dynamic pathways for Jewish learning and living. With campuses in Sherman Oaks, Beverly Hills, and Simi Valley, CA, along with distance education programs that reach learners across the nation and around the world, AJU is a private, nonprofit institution of higher education offering degree-granting and for-credit academic programs, as well as community-based (non-formal academic) learning opportunities.


Department Overview

The Information Technology department provides strategic leadership and oversight for technology across American Jewish University. Through strong partnerships with internal stakeholders and external technology providers, the department ensures that technology is secure, reliable, integrated, and aligned with the University's mission and strategic priorities.

AJU utilizes a Managed Service Provider (MSP) for day-to-day infrastructure and technical support. The Director of Information Technology & Enterprise Systems provides leadership, governance, and accountability for these outsourced services while driving technology strategy, enterprise systems, cybersecurity, business process improvement, and digital transformation across the institution.


Position Overview

The Director of Information Technology & Enterprise Systems is responsible for the strategic leadership, planning, and oversight of the University's technology and systems environment. Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer/Chief Financial Officer, this position partners with executive leadership and departments across the Institution to ensure technology investments support operational excellence, institutional growth, and an exceptional user experience.

This position is not responsible for providing day-to-day desktop support or infrastructure administration. Instead, the Director oversees the Institution’s Managed Service Provider, cybersecurity partner(s), enterprise applications, and technology vendors while leading strategic initiatives that improve business processes, system integrations, reporting, automation, and institutional effectiveness.

The Director serves as the Institution’s technology advisor, ensuring technology decisions align with organizational priorities and deliver measurable value.


Duties & Responsibilities

Strategic Technology Leadership

  • Develop and maintain the University's multi-year technology roadmap.
  • Align technology initiatives with institutional priorities and operational needs.
  • Advise executive leadership on technology trends, opportunities, risks, and investments.
  • Develop IT governance practices, standards, and policies.
  • Assist in developing and managing the annual IT operating and capital budgets.
  • Promote innovation through the thoughtful adoption of technology and AI-enabled solutions.

Managed Service Provider Oversight

  • Serve as the primary relationship manager for the University's Managed Service Provider.
  • Monitor service delivery, responsiveness, and overall performance.
  • Establish service expectations, performance metrics, and accountability measures.
  • Coordinate infrastructure projects, upgrades, cloud initiatives, and technology implementations.
  • Ensure technology services meet the needs of faculty, staff, and students.

Cybersecurity Leadership

  • Oversee the University's cybersecurity strategy in partnership with an external cybersecurity provider.
  • Coordinate vulnerability assessments, remediation efforts, security monitoring, and incident response.
  • Develop and maintain cybersecurity policies and best practices.
  • Lead security awareness and training initiatives.
  • Participate in disaster recovery and business continuity planning.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable security, privacy, and regulatory requirements.


Enterprise Systems & Applications

Provide strategic oversight for the University's enterprise technology ecosystem, including but not limited to:

  • HubSpot CRM
  • Financial Systems
  • Human Resources systems
  • Learning Management Systems
  • Event Management platforms
  • Identity management solutions
  • Project management system(s)
  • AI tools
  • Marketing and Communications management system(s)
  • Other enterprise applications

Responsibilities include:

  • Evaluating business needs and technology capabilities.
  • Improving system utilization and user adoption.
  • Identifying opportunities for automation.
  • Evaluating system integrations.
  • Recommending technology improvements.
  • Support in onboarding and offboarding access management.
  • Managing vendor relationships and software licensing.


HubSpot & CRM Leadership

Working closely with the Institution's HubSpot Administrator, this position will:

  • Partner with departments to gather business requirements.
  • Prioritize technology requests and enhancements.
  • Ensure projects remain on schedule and aligned with business needs.
  • Hold implementation teams and vendors accountable for deliverables.
  • Identify opportunities for workflow automation.
  • Improve reporting and dashboard capabilities.
  • Evaluate integrations between HubSpot and other institutional systems.
  • Promote adoption and continuous improvement across departments.

Technology Project Management

Lead and coordinate institution-wide technology initiatives, including:

  • Software implementations
  • Enterprise system upgrades
  • Cloud migrations
  • System integrations
  • Business process redesign
  • AI and workflow automation initiatives
  • Technology modernization projects

Vendor Management

  • Manage relationships with technology vendors and consultants.
  • Lead technology evaluations and RFP processes as needed.
  • Negotiate technology agreements in partnership with Finance.
  • Monitor vendor performance and service delivery.
  • Recommend technology investments that improve institutional effectiveness.

Data & Business Process Improvement

  • Partner with departments to understand operational challenges and recommend technology solutions.
  • Promote effective data governance and reporting.
  • Identify opportunities to improve efficiency through technology.
  • Support institutional reporting and decision-making through improved system utilization and data quality.

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Build collaborative relationships across all University departments.
  • Translate business needs into practical technology solutions.
  • Communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Provide regular updates to executive leadership on technology initiatives, risks, and priorities.
  • Foster a customer service-oriented approach to technology support and innovation.

Professional Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field required.
  • Master's degree or relevant technical certifications are preferred.
  • Seven (7) or more years of progressively responsible experience in information technology, enterprise systems, or digital transformation.
  • Experience managing technology vendors or outsourced technology services.
  • Experience leading or participating in enterprise software implementations or technology transformation initiatives.
  • Experience managing complex technology projects.
  • Experience working with cross-functional business teams.
  • Experience overseeing cybersecurity initiatives or working closely with cybersecurity partners.
  • Experience with CRM platforms such as HubSpot is preferred.
  • Experience in higher education or nonprofit organizations is preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Strong leadership and relationship-building skills.
  • Excellent project management capabilities.
  • Strong vendor management and negotiation skills.
  • Ability to translate business needs into technology solutions.
  • Knowledge of enterprise applications and systems integration.
  • Understanding of cloud technologies and cybersecurity best practices.
  • Experience improving business processes through technology.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Commitment to outstanding customer service.

Physical Requirements & Work Environment

  • This position operates in a professional office environment and routinely uses standard office equipment (e.g., computer, phone, copier).
  • The role requires the ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods of time and to perform repetitive tasks such as typing and data entry.
  • Must be able to communicate effectively in person, via video conferencing, and by phone.
  • Maintain regular and predicable attendance.
  • Must be able to lift, push, pull and carry objects (20 lbs.), such as office equipment, monitors, supplies and files.
  • Occasional movement throughout campus and to off-site locations may be required.

Compensation

  • This is a full-time, exempt position with a salary range of $140,000 to $160,000 annually commensurate with experience, qualifications, and demonstrated track record.
  • American Jewish University offers a comprehensive benefits package, which may include health, dental, and vision insurance; retirement plan participation; paid time off; and other employee benefits.

title: GTM Data Product Specialist Melbourne, Australia
description:

Company Description

The PaperCut Story

At PaperCut, we believe two things: great work can change the world, and a great flat white can change your morning.

Now, let’s be honest, “print management” doesn’t usually make people leap out of their chairs. But here at PaperCut, we've turned what used to be the most boring part of IT into one of the most exciting, impactful, and rewarding places to work in tech. How? Simply put: our work saves trees!

We're a B-Corp certified Australian-headquartered success story on a mission to make our customers’ tech footprint waste-free, easy, and secure. Still founder-led right here in Melbourne, our global footprint spans 195 countries, 100,000 companies, and 140 million end users (that’s roughly 1 in every 50 people on the planet!).

Job Description

We have a progressive, high-performing, and intellectually curious workforce. As we continue to scale, we’re looking for a sharp, empathetic GTM Data Product Specialist to step into a full-time role, build instant trust with our leaders, and help us navigate complex people dynamics with a cool head.

What You’ll Actually Do

PaperCut is building toward a decentralized data mesh — domains owning and producing their own data as a product, rather than one central team owning everything. GTM will be one of the first domains stepping into that model, and as GTM’s Data Product Specialists within the Commercial Operations team, you’re the person who makes that ownership real, not a central analytics team fielding requests. You’ll start from GTM’s biggest unsolved data and process problems, not from report requests. You’ll decide what “good data” looks like for Sales, Channel, Marketing, and Customer Success, build the few things that actually move those problems, and change how the domain works with data so people aren’t waiting on you for every answer.

Support Strategic Planning & Revenue Forecasting: Collaborate with Finance and GTM leadership on annual planning, revenue forecasting, quarterly business reviews (QBRs), and overall global GTM strategy.

Optimize Sales Processes & Automation: Streamline GTM workflows by turning data into an accessible product, applying AI tools and automation to reduce manual friction, and designing sales incentive/commission structures with leadership.

Own GTM’s data agenda: Identify and prioritize the 2-3 data or process problems doing the most damage to pipeline, forecast accuracy, or GTM efficiency, and drive them to resolution, not just visibility.

Drive Reporting & Performance Analytics: Use AI, SQL and data analysis tools to extract, transform, and load (ETL) data, building actionable dashboards and reports that track sales trends, KPIs, and help course‑correct performance.

Manage Tech Stack & Data Governance: Partner with IT and cross‑functional teams to integrate sales systems, maintain strict data quality controls, monitor data flows, and create team training/documentation to boost tool adoption.

Own GTM’s Semantic Layer: Define the entities, relationships, freshness requirements, and ownership for GTM’s core data objects (pipeline, funnel, forecast) so they mean the same thing everywhere they’re used — the foundation piece other domains will follow.

Assess AI and Agent Data Readiness: Before any AI tool or agent touches GTM data, evaluate whether it’s actually fit for that use case -clean, governed, and traceable -rather than letting automation run on data nobody’s validated.

What You Bring to the Table

We respect expertise, give you autonomy, and value solutions over rigid rules. You’ll thrive in this role if you bring:

Technical & Analytical Expertise: Proficiency in SQL, data modeling, warehousing concepts, and hands‑on experience using analytical tools to maintain data governance and troubleshoot quality issues.

Influence & Change: Proven ability to change how a team works with data -not just report to them, but get them to adopt new practices, even without direct authority.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: Strong capability to partner effectively across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, and IT to deliver end-to-end operational solutions.

Problem‑Solving Mindset: Excellent analytical capacity to transform raw data into clear growth strategies and actionable business insights.

Additional Information

Why Join PaperCut?

Values-Driven Culture: We live by our values: Caring, Honest, Intelligent, and Nimble (CHIN). They aren't just posters on the wall; they guide how we build products and treat each other every day.

Share in Our Success: When the company thrives, our people do too. We offer a Share the Success bonus to all permanent employees.

Real Ownership & Autonomy: Senior PaperCutters actively shape decisions through extended leadership groups and collaborative forums. Your expertise genuinely drives our direction.

Generous Benefits: Enjoy up to 18 weeks of paid parental leave, flexible hybrid working arrangements, and genuine leave options.

Authentic DEIB: Our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging initiatives are organic and run by passionate PaperCutters, not mandated from the top down.

The PaperCut Pledge

Ghosting is for Halloween. As a proud Circle Back Initiative Employer, we commit to responding to every single applicant. Our hiring process is designed to be enjoyable, thorough, and fair, giving you the space to show us the best version of yourself.

Chief Program & Strategy Officer — Position Description

Reports to:

Chief Executive Officer

Direct Reports:

Location:

New York, NY — based at NYCP’s East Harlem offices, with regular presence across program sites

About New York Common Pantry

New York Common Pantry is one of the city’s largest hunger relief organizations, providing food assistance, case management services, senior food provision, nutrition education, and hygiene services. We are a dynamic, mission-driven organization experiencing rapid growth and expansion.

NYCP is a poverty-fighting organization that reduces hunger and promotes dignity, health, and self-sufficiency by using a holistic approach. Last year, we assisted over 800,000 visitors, served over 12.5 million meals, and accessed $10.8 million in public benefits resources for our guests. Through an array of programs that we offer, we look to establish long-term stability for those we serve.

The Opportunity

The Chief Program & Strategy Officer (CPSO) is a key member of the executive leadership team and NYCP’s senior leader for programs, impact strategy, government affairs, and research. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the CPSO provides strategic leadership and oversight for all direct-service programs while helping shape the organization’s long-term growth, public policy engagement, and impact measurement. The CPSO ensures that NYCP’s programs are mission-aligned, responsive to community needs, operationally effective, and positioned for sustainable growth. The role leads a broad portfolio encompassing food programs, social services, nutrition education, program quality and innovation, research and evaluation, government relations, and strategic planning. The CPSO supervises senior program, analytics, and government affairs leaders and works collaboratively across development, finance, operations, communications, and human resources.

Key Responsibilities

Program Leadership & Service Excellence

  • Provide executive leadership and oversight for all NYCP programs and services.

  • Ensure high-quality, client-centered, equitable, and culturally responsive service delivery.

  • Strengthen integration among programs to maximize client outcomes and access to services.

  • Monitor program performance, quality, compliance, and operational effectiveness.

  • Support program leaders in developing high-performing teams and strong management practices.

  • Identify opportunities for innovation, expansion, and continuous improvement.

Strategy & Organizational Growth

  • Lead implementation of the programmatic components of NYCP’s strategic plan.

  • Advise the CEO and Board on emerging community needs, trends, opportunities, and risks.

  • Develop strategies that expand NYCP’s impact, geographic reach, partnerships, and service models.

  • Lead planning related to program growth, new initiatives, and mission impact.

  • Foster a culture that balances data-driven decision making with dignity-centered service delivery.

Government Affairs & External Partnerships

  • Develop and execute NYCP’s government affairs and public funding strategy.

  • Cultivate productive relationships with elected officials, government agencies, and public-sector partners.

  • Monitor legislative, regulatory, and funding developments affecting food security, poverty alleviation, public benefits, and nonprofit services.

  • Collaborate with executive leadership on advocacy priorities and public policy engagement.

  • Represent NYCP with government, coalition, and community stakeholders.

Research, Data & Impact

  • Oversee research, evaluation, data analytics, and impact measurement functions.

  • Establish organizational performance metrics and outcome frameworks.

  • Ensure that program and organizational decisions are informed by high-quality data and analysis.

  • Lead development of dashboards, performance reports, and insights for executive leadership and the Board.

  • Promote a culture of learning, accountability, and evidence-based practice.

Executive & Team Leadership

  • Serve as a member of the executive leadership team, contributing to organization-wide planning and decision making.

  • Supervise, mentor, and develop senior leaders across programs, analytics, and government affairs.

  • Collaborate closely with the Chief Finance & Administration Officer, Chief Development Officer, and other senior leaders.

  • Support Board committees and provide reports, analyses, and strategic recommendations.

  • Help cultivate a culture rooted in collaboration, accountability, innovation, and respect.

Qualifications

  • Advanced degree (e.g., MS, MA, MSW, PhD) in public administration, social work, public policy, public health, nonprofit management, or a related field preferred.

  • Minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience in human services, anti-poverty work, public health, community development, or a related nonprofit field.

  • Significant experience managing complex programs, multiple departments, senior-level staff, and substantial budgets.

  • Demonstrated success in strategic planning, organizational growth, and systems-level leadership.

  • Experience working with government agencies, public funding, contracts, and regulatory compliance.

  • Strong understanding of program evaluation, data analytics, and performance management.

  • Exceptional communication, relationship-building, and leadership skills.

  • Commitment to NYCP’s mission and values of dignity, health, equity, and self-sufficiency.

title: Software Engineer
description:
Company Overview

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refueling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service – spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack – from the lab to the field – we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

Headquartered in Washington, DC, with facilities across the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as Continental Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Group Overview

The Digital and Synthetic Capability Unit (D&S) is committed to providing mission-driven information solutions that seamlessly bridge the digital and physical realms. Leveraging cutting-edge technologies and advanced platforms, we empower operational readiness and elevate situational awareness across diverse domains—including air, maritime, and space.

Position Summary

Metrea is seeking a dynamic and highly motivated individual to join our software development team, building business software solutions and visualisations for the Enterprise.

What You’ll Do

  • Design, implement, and maintain well-tested, scalable code in alignment with our engineering principles and standards
  • Lead the delivery of features and enhancements to production, coordinating cross-functionally where needed
  • Architect, design, and implement microservices or monolithic solutions to improve functionality and performance
  • Apply strong understanding of system architecture and design patterns to propose and implement effective technical solutions
  • Troubleshoot, debug and resolve production issues, including conducting root cause analysis and implementing preventative improvements
  • Actively contribute to code reviews, providing constructive feedback to uphold and elevate overall code quality across the team
  • Collaborate effectively with teammates and stakeholders, contributing to technical discussions and leading design decisions
  • Proactively identify technical debt, performance bottlenecks and architectural improvements, and drive initiatives to address them
  • Consistently adhere to and help reinforce our Ways of Working, contributing to process improvements where appropriate
  • Communicate progress, risks and trade-offs clearly to the team and relevant stakeholders to ensure alignment with the product roadmap

What You Bring

  • 6 years of experience as a backend engineer with a strong focus on web development, REST APIs and software architecture ideally with the Python frameworks
  • BSc level qualification in Software Engineering or equivalent Computer Science related discipline
  • Strong understanding and practical experience of web development using Python Frameworks e.g. Django/FastAPI
  • Experience with cloud technologies, preferably Azure, and tools like Kafka, Docker, Kubernetes, Elasticsearch
  • Understanding and/or experience of team delivery in an Agile software development environment
  • Drive to learn constantly and further your knowledge
  • Strong leadership, organisational skills, proactive approach to task delivery and required documentation
  • Great interpersonal skills, able to confidently communicate and articulate technical issues to non-technical team members

Benefits

  • Private Medical Insurance
  • Subsided gym membership / plans throughWellhub
  • Electric Car scheme
  • Cycle to work scheme
  • Free lunch on office days
  • Enhanced Parental Leave
  • 30 days annual PTO plus b/h
  • Bonus Scheme
  • Personal development opportunities

WorkAuthorization/SecurityClearance

The employee will have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom and will be able to produce right to work documentation.Employee must undergo a minimum of BPSS check.Employee must be willing to sign the Official Secrets Act.

AAP/EEO Statement

Metrea is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or other characteristics protected by law.

PositionTypeandExpectedHoursofWork

This is a full-time non-exempt position with typical working hours of Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Hours and work shifts may change in accordance with department and business needs. Exempt Employees must have the ability to be on-call and available, as business needs require. Non-Exempt employees may be required to work over 40 hours per week with approval from the department manager.

WorkEnvironment

This job operates in an office setting.

Travel

This role may require occasional travel to other Metrea UK offices.

Our Firmware

At Metrea, our single core value is Rooted in Humility, and our four cornerstone attributes are Entrepreneurial, Systematic, Discerning, and Over-Deliver. These form what we call our Teammate Firmware. Just like technical firmware connects software and hardware, our Firmware is the constant interface between our mission and our people. It defines how we show up, how we work together, and how we solve complex problems.

Our team Firmware creates a web‑like, hyper‑collaborative, dynamically hierarchical way of working that helps us adapt quickly, communicate openly, and distribute decision‑making to where expertise actually lives. It enables groups to self‑organize around hard problems, shift fluidly as priorities evolve, and operate with the trust, curiosity, and discipline required in a complex mission space. This foundation allows us to deliver elegant, effective solutions and uphold our purpose: protecting our precious inheritance.

title: Senior Backend Java Developer (Microservices)
description:
We are seeking an experienced Senior Backend Java Developer with a specialised focus on microservices architecture, distributed systems, and backend engineering. In this role, you will design, build, and scale microservices-based RESTful APIs and enterprise backend components. You will focus on service communication, asynchronous messaging, optimising database interactions, and driving sound microservice design principles across the stack.

What you'll do

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable microservices and distributed backend services using Java and the Spring / Spring Boot ecosystem.
  • Implement clean microservice architectural patterns, domain-driven design, and reusable software modules.
  • Author standard OpenAPI/Swagger documentation for REST endpoints and inter-service contracts.
  • Leverage Java concurrency utilities and asynchronous messaging to ensure efficient application performance.
  • Diagnose, debug, and resolve memory leaks, thread contention, and garbage collection bottlenecks in containerised environments.
  • Design and optimise relational and NoSQL database schemas tailored for decoupled microservices.
  • Manage data persistence and transactional boundaries across distributed services using Spring Data JPA.
  • Write tuned SQL queries, establish effective database indexing, and configure caching strategies (e.g., Redis).
  • Implement robust microservice resiliency patterns including Circuit Breakers, Rate Limiting, and Retry policies.
  • Implement standard API and service security mechanisms (OAuth2, JWT authentication, authorisation, and data sanitisation).
  • Build structured logging, health checks, and application metrics using standard logging frameworks.
  • Write clean, maintainable, modular, and unit-tested microservice code using JUnit and Mockito.
  • Participate in code reviews, technical architecture reviews, and maintain test coverage across application modules.

What you'll need

  • 5+ years of hands-on software development experience using Java with deep knowledge of Collections, Streams API, Multithreading/Concurrency, and Exception Handling.
  • Strong expertise in Spring Boot, Spring Core, Spring MVC, and dependency injection paradigms.
  • Deep understanding of microservices architecture, distributed systems design principles, and RESTful architectural styles.
  • Advanced proficiency in Spring Data JPA, raw SQL query tuning, and database migration tooling.
  • Practical, hands-on experience with message brokers and event streaming architectures.
  • Solid grasp of Design Patterns, TDD/unit testing principles (JUnit, Mockito), containerization basics, and CI/CD deployment pipelines.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with service mesh technologies and cloud-native observability tools.
  • Familiarity with major cloud platforms and managed container orchestration services.
  • Experience with caching layers, distributed synchronization, and event-driven patterns.

title: Field Supervisor
description:
Field Supervisor

Water Treatment Operations | Livermore, California

CLASSIFICATION

Full-time, hourly, nonexempt

PAY RANGE

$35.00-$40.00 per hour

TRAVEL

Frequent travel required

SCHEDULE

Field-based; overtime and variable schedules may be required

Position Overview

The Field Supervisor is responsible for the safe, efficient, and professional execution of water treatment projects and field service activities. This hands-on leadership role supervises field crews and coordinates the installation, mobilization, operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and demobilization of temporary and permanent water treatment systems. The position requires strong mechanical and construction experience, effective crew leadership, sound administrative skills, and the ability to communicate professionally with customers, subcontractors, vendors, and internal project teams.

Key Responsibilities

Field Operations and Crew Leadership

  • Direct daily field activities and keep employees and subcontractors focused on assigned work, safety requirements, quality standards, and project schedules.
  • Supervise the installation, operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, mobilization, and demobilization of water treatment systems.
  • Coordinate labor, equipment, materials, tools, subcontractors, and site logistics for assigned work.
  • Review work plans, drawings, process flow diagrams, proposals, and project requirements before field execution.
  • Conduct site assessments and identify access, utility, safety, equipment, staffing, and material requirements.
  • Maintain clear daily communication with project management regarding progress, constraints, labor usage, equipment status, and customer issues.

Water Treatment and Mechanical Systems

  • Oversee and assist with pumps, filtration systems, tanks, vessels, piping, valves, hoses, instrumentation, and chemical treatment equipment.
  • Direct the fabrication, assembly, installation, repair, and modification of PVC, HDPE, steel, and other piping systems applicable to company work.
  • Diagnose mechanical and operational problems and coordinate timely repairs or corrective action.
  • Monitor system performance and confirm that equipment operates within established project and treatment requirements.

Safety and Quality

  • Lead pre-task planning, daily safety meetings, job hazard analyses, equipment inspections, and site-specific safety orientation.
  • Enforce company safety policies, customer requirements, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Exercise stop-work authority whenever unsafe conditions exist.
  • Confirm that completed installations and field activities meet project drawings, specifications, quality requirements, and company standards.
  • Report incidents, near misses, equipment damage, environmental concerns, and nonconforming work promptly.

Materials, Equipment, and Warehouse Coordination

  • Coordinate the staging, green-tagging, inspection, pulling, loading, and return of equipment, tools, and consumable materials.
  • Verify that crews have the proper equipment and materials before mobilization.
  • Track field assets, equipment condition, consumable usage, and material shortages.
  • Coordinate equipment repair, replacement, calibration, and preventive maintenance as required.

Documentation, Cost Control, and Customer Coordination

  • Complete daily field reports, labor and equipment records, inspection forms, maintenance logs, incident documentation, and customer-required reports.
  • Review employee time, cost codes, equipment usage, receipts, and other field documentation for accuracy.
  • Assist with estimating labor, equipment, materials, travel, and subcontractor requirements.
  • Monitor field costs and notify project management of potential budget or schedule impacts.
  • Document changed field conditions and provide supporting information for potential change orders.
  • Serve as the primary onsite company representative when assigned and communicate professionally with customers, inspectors, subcontractors, vendors, and internal teams.
  • Escalate commercial, contractual, technical, safety, or customer issues to the appropriate manager. Do not commit the company to additional scope, cost, or schedule changes without authorization.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Five or more years of relevant construction, environmental remediation, industrial mechanical, field service, or water treatment experience.
  • Prior experience leading field crews or coordinating daily jobsite activities.
  • Demonstrated mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting ability.
  • Experience working with pumps, piping, valves, filtration equipment, tanks, or similar process equipment.
  • Ability to read and interpret project plans, process flow diagrams, equipment manuals, proposals, and basic construction drawings.
  • Ability to prepare accurate field documentation and use Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams.
  • Valid driver's license and an acceptable motor vehicle record.
  • Ability to travel on short notice and work extended hours, nights, weekends, or emergency assignments when project conditions require.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with temporary or permanent industrial water treatment systems.
  • Experience with environmental remediation, dewatering, groundwater treatment, or construction water management.
  • OSHA 30-Hour Construction, HAZWOPER, First Aid/CPR, or other relevant safety certifications.
  • Technical degree, trade certification, or equivalent specialized training.
  • Experience estimating labor, equipment, and material requirements.

Physical Requirements and Work Environment

This position regularly works at construction, industrial, environmental, and water treatment sites. The employee may be exposed to outdoor weather, uneven terrain, noise, dust, mud, moving equipment, chemicals, and other field conditions. The position requires standing and walking for extended periods, climbing ladders or stairs, bending, kneeling, reaching, and using hand and power tools. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Compensation, Benefits, and Company Resources

  • Hourly pay range of $35.00 to $40.00. Actual starting pay will be based on relevant experience, qualifications, certifications, and job-related skills.
  • Overtime eligibility in accordance with applicable law and company policy.
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage, subject to plan eligibility and terms.
  • Paid vacation, sick leave, and company holidays, subject to applicable policy.
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions of up to 4%, subject to plan terms and eligibility.
  • Company-issued mobile phone and company credit card for authorized business use.
  • Approved business travel expenses, including applicable mileage, lodging, and per diem, reimbursed in accordance with company policy and project requirements.

Benefits and company policies may be amended from time to time. Applicable plan documents and company policies govern eligibility and coverage.

Safety Responsibility

Safety is an essential function of this position. The Field Supervisor is expected to lead by example, enforce applicable safety requirements, conduct required field safety activities, correct unsafe conditions, and exercise stop-work authority when work may endanger employees, customers, the public, the environment, or equipment.

Conditions of Employment

Any offer of employment may be conditioned upon completion of job-related pre-employment requirements, which may include verification of employment eligibility, an authorized background check, review of the candidate's motor vehicle record, and drug and alcohol testing, as permitted by applicable law and company policy.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Clear Creek Systems, Inc. provides equal employment opportunities to qualified applicants and employees without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. Reasonable accommodation is available for qualified individuals with disabilities and for other protected needs as required by law.

OTHER DUTIES This job description summarizes the primary duties of the position and is not intended to be an exhaustive list. The employee may perform other job-related duties as assigned.

title: Shipping Associate I
description:
HOW WE GOT HERE

For more than 40 years, BioIVT has evolved from a specialized biospecimen provider into a global partner to life science and diagnostic organizations. Our growth has been shaped by a consistent focus on helping researchers access the high-quality biospecimens, primary cells, ADME-Tox products, and research services they need to advance discovery, development, and medical progress.

What has remained constant throughout that history is our mission: to enable smarter science and accelerate medical breakthroughs that enhance and extend lives. Every BioIVT team member contributes to that mission, whether supporting a donor center, laboratory, commercial team, or corporate function. For employees, this means joining a company where scientific quality, operational excellence, compliance, collaboration, and customer focus all come together to support work that matters.

The primary objective for this position is to work as part of the shipping/receiving team to check in all incoming packages using company database and to ensure all outgoing packages are packed correctly and accurately on a daily basis.

Job Purpose

  • Process incoming shipment of biological materials
  • Record that incoming shipments match with expected shipments
  • Organize biological materials in appropriate freezers and refrigerators, so other team members are able to find them
  • Label outgoing biological materials with correct labels, and secure them for future shipping
  • Package materials according to all IATA PI
  • Label outgoing packages with correct labels in compliance with DOT/IATA specifications
  • Package secured biological materials with either dry ice or cold packs
  • Secure package, to make sure it travels safely towards destination
  • Constantly check and make sure that the department is stocked with supplies and packages
  • Notify Shipping Manager when supplies are needed
  • Keep warehouse neatly organized and clean at all times

Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent
  • Must have great organization and analytical skills
  • Must be comfortable working with biological materials
  • Must have great interpersonal and communication skills
  • Knowledge of Microsoft Office is a plus
  • Must be a creative and positive individual
  • You are a team player. You take your work very seriously, but not always yourself.
  • You are dedicated and reliable, high energy, and a self-starter
  • You are looking for an organization that values mission-driven, loyal individuals focused on achieving goals for those in need of our services.
  • You get things done

ALSO TRUE OF THE RIGHT PERSON

  • You are mission-driven and take pride in contributing to work that helps advance science, medical progress, and better outcomes.
  • You value collaboration and build trusted relationships by being respectful, responsive, and solutions-oriented.
  • You bring a strong sense of ownership and accountability, following through on commitments and taking pride in the quality of your work.
  • You are comfortable working in a fast-paced, growing organization where priorities can shift and good judgment, flexibility, and communication matter.
  • You care about doing things the right way, with consistency, integrity, attention to detail, and respect for quality and compliance.
  • You are curious, open to feedback, and committed to continuous improvement in how we work, learn, and grow together.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Comprehensive medical coverage with PPO/HRA and HDHP/HSA plan options.
  • Company-funded HRA or HSA contributions, depending on the medical plan elected.
  • Prescription drug coverage, virtual care through MDLIVE, and preventive care
  • Dental coverage through Cigna and vision coverage through VSP.
  • Company-paid life, AD&D, short-term disability, and long-term disability coverage.
  • Flexible spending account options, including healthcare, limited purpose, and dependent care FSAs.
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer Safe Harbor matching contributions.
  • Tuition reimbursement to support continued learning, professional growth, and career development.
  • Paid time off, company-paid holidays, employee assistance resources, travel assistance, and voluntary benefit options.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY AND BELONGING

At BioIVT, our mission to enable smarter science and accelerate medical breakthroughs is strengthened by the people who bring that work to life. We are committed to building a workplace where employees are treated with fairness, respect, and dignity, and where different experiences, perspectives, and ideas help us better serve our customers, partners, donors, and one another. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Associate Director, Government Funding
company: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
description:
Position: Associate Director, Government Funding

Department: Institutional Giving, Advancement & Innovation

Role Overview: An integral leader and subject matter expert in Advancement & Innovation (A&I), the Associate Director, Government Funding owns Lincoln Center’s government fundraising function end to end — strategy, goal setting, agency relationships, applications, reporting, compliance systems, and the internal structure that keeps the work moving. The portfolio spans city, state, and federal sources (DCLA, NYSCA, ESD, DASNY, USDOE, EDC, DDC) and currently carries 8–10 active or pending awards representing more than $40M in committed and expected funds, weighted toward multimillion-dollar capital agreements alongside operating grants.

The Associate Director carries complex applications, requisitions, and compliance obligations personally while supervising one coordinator and contributing to cross-functional strategy. The ideal candidate has an advanced command of government funding at the city, state, and federal level — ideally at an arts or cultural institution — and deep, hands-on experience with government capital funding from application through drawdown and closeout. They are meticulously detail-oriented, systems-minded, comfortable carrying personal compliance responsibility under federal Uniform Guidance and state and city procurement law, and able to hold multiple shifting priorities across a highly matrixed environment.

What you’ll get to do here:

  • Own government fundraising strategy and goal setting across operating and capital lines, and supports the setting of annual revenue targets for the function.
  • Serve as agency-level liaison for every funding stream, managing relationships with program officers at several agencies, and stay abreast of elected official engagement and overlap, which sits with the Government Relations team.
  • Lead the full lifecycle for each opportunity — strategy, project selection, narrative, budgets, certifications and assurances, and attachments — and personally drive the most complex city, state, and federal capital and operating applications to submission.
  • Manage post-award execution: contract review and negotiation routing with LCPA’s in-house counsel, internal recordkeeping, kickoff meetings with project staff, and standing up the workstreams each new award opens.
  • Own compliance across the portfolio, including procurement and MWBE documentation, requisition and reimbursement processing, drawdowns, monthly certifications, quarterly reconciliations, federal financial and programmatic reporting, and audit readiness, in partnership with other LCPA business units.
  • Shepherd capital payment requisitions from start to finish, coordinating financial backup from project and finance partners.
  • In partnership with Coordinator, maintain city, state, and federal prequalification and registration systems (SAM.gov, login.gov, PIP, state and city portals).
  • Supervise the Government Funding Coordinator, delegating boilerplate proposals and reports, training on portals and systems, and serving as expert reviewer and sounding board.
  • Run and iterate on the internal operating rhythm of the function working cross-departmentally and cross-functionally on structures needed for each distinct award, aligning budgets, contracts, compliance, and deliverables across every stakeholder.
  • Steward funders at the agency level in coordination with A&I Operations, managing crediting and recognition requirements.
  • Monitor the landscape for new city, state, and federal opportunities, assess fit and feasibility, and set strategy for pursuit.

You’ll be a fit if you bring:

  • 5–7+ years of government grants experience, with a demonstrated record leading large, complex city, state, and federal applications, awards, and post-award compliance — ideally at an arts or cultural institution.
  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in Public Administration, Nonprofit Management, or a related field a plus.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills in a highly matrixed environment, and a genuine enthusiasm for Lincoln Center’s mission.

title: Casus- en Procesregisseur
description:
Casus- en Procesregisseur

Als Casus- en Procesregisseur begeleid je inwoners en gezinnen met complexe problematiek waarbij meerdere leefgebieden en organisaties betrokken zijn. Je analyseert de situatie, brengt samenhang aan in de ondersteuning en zorgt dat er een duidelijk integraal plan ligt. Veiligheid, passende hulpverlening en duurzame verandering staan daarbij centraal.

Je voert regie op het volledige proces, bewaakt de voortgang en zorgt dat betrokken professionals hun inzet goed op elkaar afstemmen. Wanneer de veiligheid onvoldoende verbetert of een casus vastloopt, weet je wanneer je moet bijsturen, escaleren of opschalen naar bijvoorbeeld Veilig Thuis of Jeugdbescherming.

Wat je gaat doen:

  • Analyseren van de problematiek, mogelijkheden en ondersteuningsbehoefte van inwoners en gezinnen;

  • Opstellen en bewaken van integrale plannen;

  • Opstellen van veiligheidsplannen en bewaken van veiligheidsafspraken en bodemeisen;

  • Toepassen van ARIJ en/of ZRM binnen de casuïstiek;

  • Bepalen en inzetten van passende zorg en hulpverlening;

  • Voeren van casus- en procesregie rondom complexe situaties;

  • Monitoren van ingezette zorg, hulpverlening en onderwijs, onder andere via uitvoeringsoverleggen (UVO’s);

  • Bijstellen van de ingezette ondersteuning wanneer de situatie daarom vraagt;

  • Opstellen van borgingsplannen en organiseren van borgingsafspraken;

  • Borgen van de veranderingen die inwoners en gezinnen hebben doorgemaakt;

  • Escaleren van vastlopende casuïstiek naar de coördinator;

  • Consulteren en waar nodig opschalen naar Jeugdbescherming of Veilig Thuis wanneer de onveiligheid onvoldoende afneemt;

  • Deelnemen aan casuïstiekoverleggen en zelfstandig inbrengen van casussen;

  • Voorbereiden van casuïstiekoverleggen en caseloadbesprekingen;

  • Samenwerken met inwoners, gezinnen en betrokken professionals en ketenpartners.

Wat jij meebrengt:

  • Hbo-werk- en -denkniveau;

  • Een afgeronde relevante vakgerichte opleiding, zoals Social Work;

  • Een geldige SKJ-registratie;

  • Werkervaring binnen het vakgebied;

  • Kennis van en ervaring met het voeren van casus- en procesregie;

  • Kennis van de Meldcode huiselijk geweld en kindermishandeling;

  • Kennis van de sociale kaart;

  • Juridische kennis op het gebied van strafrecht, civiel recht en bestuursrecht is een pré;

  • Je bent bereid een VOG aan te leveren;

  • Je kunt buiten bestaande kaders denken en handelt praktisch en oplossingsgericht;

  • Je bent politiek-bestuurlijk en omgevingssensitief;

  • Je beschikt over sterke mondelinge en schriftelijke communicatieve vaardigheden;

  • Je bent stressbestendig en behoudt overzicht in complexe situaties;

  • Je bent verbindend, resultaatgericht en beschikt over een hands-on mentaliteit;

  • Je werkt gemakkelijk samen en kunt flexibel inspelen op veranderende omstandigheden.

Wij bieden:

  • Een uitdagende en afwisselende baan met veel verantwoordelijkheid.

  • Een fijne werkomgeving met enthousiaste en betrokken collega’s.

  • Een salaris volgens de gemeente CAO.

  • Ruimte voor persoonlijke en professionele ontwikkeling via cursussen, trainingen en doorgroeimogelijkheden binnen de organisatie.

  • Toegang tot ons online leerplatform om jezelf te blijven ontwikkelen.

  • Gezellige clubdagen met inhoudelijke workshops.

  • Jaarlijks een zomerfeest en een kerstfeest om samen successen te vieren.

title: Management Consulting, Head of AI and Technology
description:
Role purpose

The Head of AI and Technology is accountable for the direction, delivery and adoption of AI across Teneo Management Consulting and for ensuring that its broader technology environment supports the needs of the business. The role sets the AI strategy and investment priorities, leads the AI Engineering team, owns the strategy and priorities for Management Consulting-specific technology, software, data, knowledge-management workflows and subscriptions, and acts as the principal Management Consulting stakeholder for Teneo IT on centrally managed technology, data platforms and services.

The role connects Management Consulting's priorities with Teneo's central AI team, Teneo IT and other control and enabling functions. It translates business needs into Management Consulting-owned AI and technology initiatives or clear requirements for central teams, moves high-value AI and software solutions from experimentation into reliable use, and gives consultants the skills and support required to use approved AI tools effectively.

It is primarily an internal capability role. The role is accountable for the allocation and utilisation of the AI Engineering team, including support for selected client engagements, and for the Management Consulting-specific AI and broader technology within its remit. Teneo IT and Teneo's central AI team remain accountable for the centrally managed services and capabilities, while Management Consulting engagement leaders retain accountability for client relationships, overall engagement delivery and revenue targets.

Key responsibilities

AI strategy and priorities

  • Own the Management Consulting AI strategy, roadmap and priorities, aligned with the business strategy and Teneo-wide AI direction. Consult Teneo's central AI team on new solutions to reuse firm-wide capabilities, avoid duplication and manage enterprise dependencies.
  • Identify and assess AI opportunities across consulting delivery, business development, proposition development, internal operations and knowledge work.
  • Own prioritisation of AI opportunities and allocation of AI Engineering capacity within the approved budget, considering value, feasibility, risk, reuse potential, capacity and cost. Escalate material investments, major reprioritisation and strategically sensitive work to Management Consulting leadership.
  • Develop business cases and recommend whether Management Consulting should build, buy, partner, reuse a central capability, scale an existing initiative or stop further investment.
  • Define outcome measures for priority AI initiatives and report progress, realised value, adoption, spend, risks and dependencies to Management Consulting and wider Teneo leadership.

Leadership of the AI Engineering team

  • Lead the day-to-day work of the Management Consulting AI Engineering team, including objectives, prioritisation, resource allocation, workforce planning, utilisation, delivery oversight and performance management.
  • Balance the team's capacity across client engagements, internal tooling development, enablement of the broader MC team, and technical capability improvement, while maintaining sustainable workloads.
  • Set and enforce engineering and product standards for Management Consulting AI solutions, consistent with mandatory Teneo-wide architecture, AI, security and technology standards.
  • Define clear demand, resourcing and decision-making processes between the AI Engineering team and key stakeholders, including Resourcing, Operations, Finance, project leads and the wider client-facing team.
  • Build the team's capability through recruitment, coaching, feedback, career development and targeted use of external partners where justified.
  • Maintain high practical AI fluency and sufficient technical understanding to create simple prototypes, automations and demonstrations, evaluate their outputs and translate business needs into clear engineering requirements, without becoming the bottleneck for implementation.

AI service lifecycle

  • Oversee the path from discovery and prototyping to production, adoption, support and retirement for Management Consulting AI solutions.
  • Ensure solutions are designed for reuse where appropriate and integrate with approved data, identity, security and collaboration environments.
  • Establish proportionate evaluation and monitoring for quality, reliability, user experience, cost and risk, including controls for generative AI outputs.
  • Define ownership and support arrangements before launch, and ensure that technical debt, maintenance and business continuity inform investment and prioritisation decisions.

Business partnership and consulting integration

  • Partner with Management Consulting leadership and practice leads to translate business priorities into a focused AI agenda and secure decisions on investment, risk and operating change.
  • Support proposition and methodology development by identifying where approved AI capabilities can improve the quality, speed or differentiation of consulting work.
  • Advise case teams on feasible and responsible use of AI, deploying the AI Engineering team where specialist support is justified. Own the team's allocation and utilisation; engagement leaders remain accountable for client relationships and engagement delivery.
  • Represent Management Consulting in relevant Teneo forums and maintain productive relationships with external technology and delivery partners.

Teneo IT partnership and centrally managed technology

  • Act as the principal Management Consulting stakeholder for Teneo IT, representing the business's needs and priorities in relation to centrally managed technology, data platforms and services.
  • Translate Management Consulting requirements into clear input for firm-wide technology strategy, roadmaps and investment decisions, and communicate central plans, constraints and decisions to Management Consulting leadership.
  • Coordinate with Teneo IT and relevant central functions on architecture, integration, identity and access, hosting, resilience, service support and technology changes affecting Management Consulting.
  • Monitor the performance of centrally managed services within Management Consulting, escalating material issues and working with Teneo IT to agree appropriate action.

Management Consulting technology, knowledge management and subscriptions

  • Own the strategy, roadmap and priorities for Management Consulting-specific technology, software, data and subscriptions, aligned with business and AI priorities and Teneo-wide standards.
  • Maintain a coherent view of Management Consulting applications, data sources, knowledge assets, licences and subscriptions, reducing duplication and addressing material capability gaps.
  • Own selected technology-enabled knowledge-management workflows, including the capture, organisation, permissioning, retrieval and reuse of knowledge for consulting and AI-enabled workflows.
  • Work with client-facing teams and designated knowledge owners to establish clear accountability for the quality, permissions and appropriate use of knowledge assets, while acting as a key stakeholder in wider knowledge-management decisions.
  • Lead business cases, supplier evaluation, procurement and renewals for Management Consulting-specific tools and services. Manage approved expenditure, licences and consumption within delegated authority and the relevant central approval processes.

Training enablement and adoption

  • Set the AI capability-building plan for Management Consulting, based on the needs of different roles, practices and levels of experience.
  • Direct practical training, guidance, demonstrations, office hours and communities of practice that help colleagues apply approved tools to real consulting workflows.
  • Expand the network of leaders and super-users who can reinforce good practice, surface demand and support adoption within their teams.
  • Measure confidence, active use, quality and workflow impact, and adapt the enablement programme where training does not translate into sustained behaviour change.
  • Maintain clear communication on available tools, expected use, limitations, new releases and routes for support.

Responsible AI governance and risk

  • Consult Teneo's central AI team on proposed solutions to identify existing capabilities, avoid duplication and maintain alignment with Teneo-wide AI direction.
  • Work with Cyber Security, Risk, Legal and IT to translate firm-wide requirements into practical delivery and usage controls.
  • Ensure new AI solutions receive the required Cyber Security and Risk approvals prior to implementation, with clear records of decisions, exceptions and accountable owners.
  • Promote safe handling of client and firm information and address emerging model, vendor and regulatory risks as the technology changes.

Experience and capabilities

  • Substantial experience setting and delivering an AI and technology strategy in a professional services, consulting or similarly knowledge-intensive environment.
  • Demonstrable experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams and taking AI or software products from discovery into secure, supported production use, with the judgement to challenge decisions on architecture, integration, evaluation, security and operational support.
  • High practical AI fluency, demonstrated through regular use of generative AI tools and the ability to create and evaluate simple prototypes, automations or workflows. Production coding experience is not required, but the candidate must recognise when specialist engineering support is needed.
  • Evidence of converting ambiguous business needs into prioritised initiatives, investment cases, delivery plans and measurable outcomes.
  • Experience of technology and data governance, including responsible AI, information security, privacy, vendor risk and approval processes.
  • Experience improving data or knowledge-management workflows in a professional services or similarly knowledge-intensive environment, particularly where these support enterprise search, knowledge retrieval or AI-enabled use.
  • Commercial judgement in build-versus-buy decisions, vendor selection, budgets, licences, subscriptions and consumption management.
  • Experience designing enablement or change programmes that produce sustained adoption, rather than training attendance alone.
  • Experience representing a business unit in relation to centrally managed technology services, translating requirements, explaining technical choices clearly and influencing enterprise technology priorities.
  • Strong people leader: sets direction, develops talent, gives clear feedback and builds effective teams.

title: Delivery Consultant - Agentic AI Full Stack Developer, AWS Professional Services
description:
Description

Are you a builder with a strong software development background who gets excited about designing and delivering end-to-end applications powered by Generative AI? Are you interested in helping the largest and most innovative companies in Australia and New Zealand build their next generation of digital products? Come join Amazon Web Services (AWS) Professional Services as a Delivery Consultant specializing in Agentic AI Full Stack Development. In this role, you will leverage your full-stack software development expertise to architect and deliver cloud-native GenAI solutions for our customers, combining hands‑on coding with consulting best practices.

We are seeking a hands‑on Senior Consultant with deep software engineering, Generative AI, and cloud architecture expertise to deliver complex technical consulting engagements within AWS Professional Services. The ideal candidate will combine strong technical depth with proven engineering capabilities, having both the software development background to work with complex architectures and code, and the curiosity to invent on behalf of our customers using AWS services. You develop using agentic tools and services – AI‑powered coding assistants, agentic IDEs, and AI‑driven development workflows are part of how you build every day. You understand how to design and orchestrate AI agents, work with protocols like MCP and A2A, and build autonomous systems using services like Amazon Bedrock. You'll work directly with customers to deliver innovative AWS solutions, applying your technical expertise to ensure successful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and security.

Key job responsibilities

  • Full-Stack Development - Design, build, and ship cloud-native applications end-to-end. Develop responsive frontend interfaces (e.g., React, Next.js, Vue) and scalable backend services (e.g., Python, TypeScript, Java), deploying on AWS with infrastructure as code and CI/CD pipelines.
  • AI‑Assisted Software Development - Use AI-powered development tools as part of your daily workflow. Champion agentic software development methodologies - leveraging AI to accelerate coding, testing, code review, and delivery.
  • Agentic Development - Design and implement AI agent architectures and multi-agent systems. Work with emerging protocols (e.g., MCP, A2A) and orchestration frameworks to build autonomous and semi-autonomous AI workflows that solve real customer problems.
  • Solution Delivery - Work directly with customers to understand requirements, architect solutions, and deliver working software. Build distributed systems, modernize existing applications, and implement best practices across cloud environments.
  • Technical Leadership - Guide customer and partner teams on software engineering best practices, software architecture decisions, and code quality. Conduct code reviews, mentor developers, and ensure solutions meet security and operational excellence standards.

A day in the life

AWS Professional Services includes experts from across AWS who help our customers design, build, operate, and secure their cloud environments. Customers innovate with AWS Professional Services, upskill with AWS Training and Certification, optimize with AWS Support and Managed Services, and meet objectives with AWS Security Assurance Services. Our expertise and emerging technologies include AWS Partners, AWS Sovereign Cloud, AWS International Product, and the Generative AI Innovation Center. You’ll join a diverse team of technical experts in dozens of countries who help customers achieve more with the AWS cloud.

About The Team

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Basic Qualifications

  • Knowledge of primary AWS services (EC2, ELB, RDS, VPC, Route53, S3) with 5+ years of cloud architecture and solution implementation experience on AWS or comparable platforms, including deploying across distributed computing environments.
  • 5+ years of hands‑on development with modern programming languages (e.g., TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, Kotlin, .NET).
  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code (e.g., AWS CDK, CloudFormation, Terraform), CI/CD pipelines, and DevOps practices.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools as part of the software development workflow.
  • Proven experience implementing AWS services in a variety of distributed computing environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience and technical expertise (design and implementation) in cloud computing technologies
  • Experience leading the design, development and deployment of business software at scale or recent hands‑on technology infrastructure, network, compute, storage, and virtualization experience
  • Understanding of AI agent architectures, orchestration patterns, and emerging protocols (e.g., MCP, A2A) with hands‑on experience building multi‑agent systems and applications that integrate generative AI / LLM capabilities (e.g., RAG, chat interfaces, agent workflows, LLM-powered features).
  • Experience with agentic software development methodologies — using AI agents to accelerate development workflows including coding, testing, debugging, and code review.
  • Understanding of API design and implementation (REST, GraphQL, gRPC) and identity protocols (OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0).
  • Hands‑on experience with containerization and orchestration (e.g., Docker, Amazon ECS, Kubernetes), distributed systems, event‑driven architectures, and microservices patterns at scale.
  • Familiarity with observability and monitoring practices (e.g., OpenTelemetry, CloudWatch, Datadog) with a focus on operational excellence.

title: Management Consulting, Head of AI and Technology
description:
Role purpose

The Head of AI and Technology is accountable for the direction, delivery and adoption of AI across Teneo Management Consulting and for ensuring that its broader technology environment supports the needs of the business. The role sets the AI strategy and investment priorities, leads the AI Engineering team, owns the strategy and priorities for Management Consulting-specific technology, software, data, knowledge-management workflows and subscriptions, and acts as the principal Management Consulting stakeholder for Teneo IT on centrally managed technology, data platforms and services.

The role connects Management Consulting's priorities with Teneo's central AI team, Teneo IT and other control and enabling functions. It translates business needs into Management Consulting-owned AI and technology initiatives or clear requirements for central teams, moves high-value AI and software solutions from experimentation into reliable use, and gives consultants the skills and support required to use approved AI tools effectively.

It is primarily an internal capability role. The role is accountable for the allocation and utilisation of the AI Engineering team, including support for selected client engagements, and for the Management Consulting-specific AI and broader technology within its remit. Teneo IT and Teneo's central AI team remain accountable for the centrally managed services and capabilities, while Management Consulting engagement leaders retain accountability for client relationships, overall engagement delivery and revenue targets.

Key responsibilities

AI strategy and priorities

  • Own the Management Consulting AI strategy, roadmap and priorities, aligned with the business strategy and Teneo-wide AI direction. Consult Teneo's central AI team on new solutions to reuse firm-wide capabilities, avoid duplication and manage enterprise dependencies.
  • Identify and assess AI opportunities across consulting delivery, business development, proposition development, internal operations and knowledge work.
  • Own prioritisation of AI opportunities and allocation of AI Engineering capacity within the approved budget, considering value, feasibility, risk, reuse potential, capacity and cost. Escalate material investments, major reprioritisation and strategically sensitive work to Management Consulting leadership.
  • Develop business cases and recommend whether Management Consulting should build, buy, partner, reuse a central capability, scale an existing initiative or stop further investment.
  • Define outcome measures for priority AI initiatives and report progress, realised value, adoption, spend, risks and dependencies to Management Consulting and wider Teneo leadership.

Leadership of the AI Engineering team

  • Lead the day-to-day work of the Management Consulting AI Engineering team, including objectives, prioritisation, resource allocation, workforce planning, utilisation, delivery oversight and performance management.
  • Balance the team's capacity across client engagements, internal tooling development, enablement of the broader MC team, and technical capability improvement, while maintaining sustainable workloads.
  • Set and enforce engineering and product standards for Management Consulting AI solutions, consistent with mandatory Teneo-wide architecture, AI, security and technology standards.
  • Define clear demand, resourcing and decision-making processes between the AI Engineering team and key stakeholders, including Resourcing, Operations, Finance, project leads and the wider client-facing team.
  • Build the team's capability through recruitment, coaching, feedback, career development and targeted use of external partners where justified.
  • Maintain high practical AI fluency and sufficient technical understanding to create simple prototypes, automations and demonstrations, evaluate their outputs and translate business needs into clear engineering requirements, without becoming the bottleneck for implementation.

AI service lifecycle

  • Oversee the path from discovery and prototyping to production, adoption, support and retirement for Management Consulting AI solutions.
  • Ensure solutions are designed for reuse where appropriate and integrate with approved data, identity, security and collaboration environments.
  • Establish proportionate evaluation and monitoring for quality, reliability, user experience, cost and risk, including controls for generative AI outputs.
  • Define ownership and support arrangements before launch, and ensure that technical debt, maintenance and business continuity inform investment and prioritisation decisions.

Business partnership and consulting integration

  • Partner with Management Consulting leadership and practice leads to translate business priorities into a focused AI agenda and secure decisions on investment, risk and operating change.
  • Support proposition and methodology development by identifying where approved AI capabilities can improve the quality, speed or differentiation of consulting work.
  • Advise case teams on feasible and responsible use of AI, deploying the AI Engineering team where specialist support is justified. Own the team's allocation and utilisation; engagement leaders remain accountable for client relationships and engagement delivery.
  • Represent Management Consulting in relevant Teneo forums and maintain productive relationships with external technology and delivery partners.

Teneo IT partnership and centrally managed technology

  • Act as the principal Management Consulting stakeholder for Teneo IT, representing the business's needs and priorities in relation to centrally managed technology, data platforms and services.
  • Translate Management Consulting requirements into clear input for firm-wide technology strategy, roadmaps and investment decisions, and communicate central plans, constraints and decisions to Management Consulting leadership.
  • Coordinate with Teneo IT and relevant central functions on architecture, integration, identity and access, hosting, resilience, service support and technology changes affecting Management Consulting.
  • Monitor the performance of centrally managed services within Management Consulting, escalating material issues and working with Teneo IT to agree appropriate action.

Management Consulting technology, knowledge management and subscriptions

  • Own the strategy, roadmap and priorities for Management Consulting-specific technology, software, data and subscriptions, aligned with business and AI priorities and Teneo-wide standards.
  • Maintain a coherent view of Management Consulting applications, data sources, knowledge assets, licences and subscriptions, reducing duplication and addressing material capability gaps.
  • Own selected technology-enabled knowledge-management workflows, including the capture, organisation, permissioning, retrieval and reuse of knowledge for consulting and AI-enabled workflows.
  • Work with client-facing teams and designated knowledge owners to establish clear accountability for the quality, permissions and appropriate use of knowledge assets, while acting as a key stakeholder in wider knowledge-management decisions.
  • Lead business cases, supplier evaluation, procurement and renewals for Management Consulting-specific tools and services. Manage approved expenditure, licences and consumption within delegated authority and the relevant central approval processes.

Training enablement and adoption

  • Set the AI capability-building plan for Management Consulting, based on the needs of different roles, practices and levels of experience.
  • Direct practical training, guidance, demonstrations, office hours and communities of practice that help colleagues apply approved tools to real consulting workflows.
  • Expand the network of leaders and super-users who can reinforce good practice, surface demand and support adoption within their teams.
  • Measure confidence, active use, quality and workflow impact, and adapt the enablement programme where training does not translate into sustained behaviour change.
  • Maintain clear communication on available tools, expected use, limitations, new releases and routes for support.

Responsible AI governance and risk

  • Consult Teneo's central AI team on proposed solutions to identify existing capabilities, avoid duplication and maintain alignment with Teneo-wide AI direction.
  • Work with Cyber Security, Risk, Legal and IT to translate firm-wide requirements into practical delivery and usage controls.
  • Ensure new AI solutions receive the required Cyber Security and Risk approvals prior to implementation, with clear records of decisions, exceptions and accountable owners.
  • Promote safe handling of client and firm information and address emerging model, vendor and regulatory risks as the technology changes.

Experience and capabilities

  • Substantial experience setting and delivering an AI and technology strategy in a professional services, consulting or similarly knowledge-intensive environment.
  • Demonstrable experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams and taking AI or software products from discovery into secure, supported production use, with the judgement to challenge decisions on architecture, integration, evaluation, security and operational support.
  • High practical AI fluency, demonstrated through regular use of generative AI tools and the ability to create and evaluate simple prototypes, automations or workflows. Production coding experience is not required, but the candidate must recognise when specialist engineering support is needed.
  • Evidence of converting ambiguous business needs into prioritised initiatives, investment cases, delivery plans and measurable outcomes.
  • Experience of technology and data governance, including responsible AI, information security, privacy, vendor risk and approval processes.
  • Experience improving data or knowledge-management workflows in a professional services or similarly knowledge-intensive environment, particularly where these support enterprise search, knowledge retrieval or AI-enabled use.
  • Commercial judgement in build-versus-buy decisions, vendor selection, budgets, licences, subscriptions and consumption management.
  • Experience designing enablement or change programmes that produce sustained adoption, rather than training attendance alone.
  • Experience representing a business unit in relation to centrally managed technology services, translating requirements, explaining technical choices clearly and influencing enterprise technology priorities.
  • Strong people leader: sets direction, develops talent, gives clear feedback and builds effective teams.
